EPS-fault siren latency ≤ 1.26 s worst case from fault onset (T-28; corrected 2026-10-13 from ≈ 1.14 s: the speaker sounds only on every other 8 Hz tick) exceeds the SG-02 1 s warning budget (§3.7). TSR-516's ≤ 0.5 s after detection is met (≤ 0.26 s) only because WP-S-02 v0.14 defines detection as the 1 s persistence; measured from the first fault frame it is not. Caused by the maintainer decision of 2026-10-12 (persistent faults only, 1 s; EPS-fault impact record §7). Options: shorten the persistence (e.g. 0.7 s), or justify that LKA actuation is already refused from the first fault frame (lateral authority removed at onset; the warning is for a lasting loss). Decision needed. No requirement changed here (added 2026-10-12)

Heartbeat loss when authority ended within the 5 s before it: TSR-516(a) asks for the siren ≤ 0.5 s after detection, but the fast siren (T-07a) sounds only when authority is granted at the revocation; this case keeps the 1 Hz siren at 4–5 s (T-07). Decide whether the case needs a warning within the SG-02 budget (the driver has already seen the disengagement) and align TSR-516(a) or the firmware. No requirement changed here (added 2026-10-13)

findings.title: Authoritative clause universe is not yet accessible
findings.basis: Documentary finding; ISO normative verdict pending source verification
findings.analysis: Repository cross-references cannot establish that every requirement, table and annex is covered. User confirms licensed 2018 source exists; the supplied Windows search link is not accessible from this cloud machine.

findings.title: The current staffing decision blocks the planned governance gate
findings.basis: Documentary finding; ISO normative verdict pending source verification
findings.analysis: The safety plan explicitly says the no-assessor decision prevents G0 under its existing CR-01/CR-03 plan. AI review cannot silently satisfy that requirement.
findings.action: Reconcile staffing decision and confirmation plan; appoint qualified reviewers and assessor or formally re-plan without claiming gate completion.
findings.closure: Named roles, competence/conflict declarations, approved plan and signed confirmation records.

evidence.excerpt: | OI-3 | Engage an external functional safety assessor (D-06) and agree scope and schedule. The lead answered on 2026-10-14: no assessor for now (DQ-009 option C). While that holds, G0 cannot pass, because CR-01 and CR-03 are due at G0 at I3 (WP-M-06 §9); the plan must be re-planned or the answer revisited | PM | G0 |

findings.title: AI-generated review has no independent verification credit under the project rules
findings.basis: Documentary finding; ISO normative verdict pending source verification
findings.analysis: This workbook is an assessment aid. The project explicitly assigns AI audits I0; this deliverable cannot be counted as an I1/I3 confirmation or signed FSA.
findings.action: Arrange human review appropriate to the approved ASIL and maintain a separate evidence acceptance trail.
findings.closure: Qualified reviewer signs baseline-specific findings and disposition; independence is evidenced.

evidence.excerpt: - AI drafting is not a verification activity. An AI-produced audit or checklist run (for example RR-2026-005…008) is an author-side pre-review audit at I0. It gives no review credit at I1 or above.

findings.title: Safety integrity ratings depend on unverified OEM/driver assumptions
findings.basis: Documentary finding; ISO normative verdict pending source verification
findings.analysis: The HARA explicitly increases the steering case from C to D if credited EPS assumptions are not verified. Current lower targets cannot be treated as established.
findings.action: Verify assumptions per exact ECU/configuration; challenge S/E/C rationale and document both credited and failed-assumption variants.
findings.closure: Approved HARA, witnessed characterization records, configuration binding and independent confirmation.

evidence.excerpt: | HE-01.1 | OS-03 undivided road, oncoming traffic, 60–90 km/h | Departure into the oncoming lane; head-on collision | S3 | E4 | C2 ⚠ | C | S3: head-on at combined speeds > 100 km/h, life-threatening. E4: undivided roads make up a large share of driving. C2 ⚠: credits AOU-01/AOU-02 (EPS limits LKA torque to an overpowerable level). A supervising driver with hands near the wheel corrects a sustained limited-torque deviation within 1 s in most cases (≥ 90%). If AOU-01/02 are not verified: C3 → ASIL D |

findings.title: Reduced-authority strategy is a recommendation rather than an approved safety basis
findings.basis: Documentary finding; ISO normative verdict pending source verification
findings.analysis: Option (c) requires measured controllability and speed-dependent limits before re-rating; ASIL reduction and decomposition are different arguments.
findings.action: Record the strategy decision, validate limits and re-rate only after justified controllability; preserve original integrity demands until then.
findings.closure: Signed strategy plus validated limit data, revised allocations and confirmed HARA.

evidence.excerpt: SG-01 at ASIL C (D if the EPS assumptions fail) drives the integrity of the envelope. The HARA lists three options. This section evaluates them and recommends one. The decision belongs to the maintainer (acting safety manager); this section is a recommendation.

findings.title: Assessment configuration is not fully identified
findings.basis: Documentary finding; ISO normative verdict pending source verification
findings.analysis: VIN, ECU firmware, device revision and harness identity are still open items. A generation-level vehicle label is insufficient to bind physical evidence.
findings.action: Freeze an assessed configuration including hardware serial/revision, ECU firmware, software/submodules, models and calibration.
findings.closure: Complete configuration record and matching manifests for every cited result.

evidence.excerpt: | OI-1 | Record the reference vehicle VIN, ECU firmware versions (fingerprint query output), options, tyre size | Maintainer | G1 |

findings.title: Part-specific hardware metrics are not demonstrated
findings.basis: Documentary finding; ISO normative verdict pending source verification
findings.analysis: WP-H-04 lacks BOM-based calculation; WP-H-03 has generic estimates, not part-specific compliance evidence. Generic results cannot close the metric obligation.
findings.action: Acquire BOM/mission profile/failure-rate evidence, validate fault classes and diagnostic coverage, compute per-goal metrics and sensitivity.
findings.closure: Reviewed FMEDA and reproducible part-specific SPFM/LFM/PMHF with traceable inputs and valid targets.

evidence.excerpt: | 5 Calculation | Cannot be computed: no BOM |

findings.title: Generic FMEDA values must remain separated from demonstrated metrics
findings.basis: Documentary finding; ISO normative verdict pending source verification
findings.analysis: Generic SG-01 SPFM 96.9% and SG-07 86.8% miss the document targets; improved planned-measure values assume implementation and coverage. These are planning warnings, not verified pass/fail results.
findings.action: Label estimates, planned architecture and measured results separately; reconcile WP-H-03 with WP-H-04/05 and confirm target authority.
findings.closure: One configuration-consistent calculation set; planned mechanisms excluded until coverage is substantiated.

evidence.excerpt: The rates are order-of-magnitude estimates per part type, not values looked up for the actual parts. The results show where the architecture falls short. They are not evidence of compliance.

findings.title: Documented warning latency exceeds the stated warning budget
findings.basis: Documentary finding; ISO normative verdict pending source verification
findings.analysis: The document records up to 1.26 s against SG-02 1 s; starting the clock after 1 s persistence can conceal end-to-end delay. This is a documented requirement discrepancy, not a new hardware measurement.
findings.action: Resolve the requirement/detection-time definition and measure fault onset through actuation removal and audible warning under worst-case load.
findings.closure: Approved consistent timing budget and witnessed end-to-end traces including tolerance and jitter.

evidence.excerpt: | OI-8 | EPS-fault siren latency ≤ 1.26 s worst case from fault onset (T-28; corrected 2026-10-13 from ≈ 1.14 s: the speaker sounds only on every other 8 Hz tick) exceeds the SG-02 1 s warning budget (§3.7). TSR-516's ≤ 0.5 s after detection is met (≤ 0.26 s) only because WP-S-02 v0.14 defines detection as the 1 s persistence; measured from the first fault frame it is not. Caused by the maintainer decision of 2026-10-12 (persistent faults only, 1 s; EPS-fault impact record §7). Options: shorten the persistence (e.g. 0.7 s), or justify that LKA actuation is already refused from the first fault frame (lateral authority removed at onset; the warning is for a lasting loss). Decision needed. No requirement changed here (added 2026-10-12) | Safety manager | G2 |

findings.title: Curve-bound time to departure is shorter than assumed driver reaction
findings.basis: Documentary finding; ISO normative verdict pending source verification
findings.analysis: The repository estimates roughly 0.7 s at the ODD bound and itself requests a controllability re-rating or tighter ODD. Driver supervision is not an automatic mitigation.
findings.action: Validate dynamics at the boundary; revise ODD, authority or hazard controllability and flow changes through FSC/TSRs.
findings.closure: Measured validated model, updated ODD and accepted HARA/FTTI rationale.

evidence.excerpt: The physical time to departure in a curve (≈ 0.7 s) is shorter than driver reaction, so SG-02 in curves at the ODD bound relies on the warning being given at once and on torque being ramped rather than cut (FSR-02.04). Warning budget: ≤ 0.5 s detection + ≤ 0.5 s to warning (FSC §8) is not sufficient alone for curves at the ODD bound; it is sufficient on straight roads and gentle curves. This is a controllability and ODD question (OI-2), recorded for the HARA owner. For SG-06 (stationary lead at 30 m/s, decel need 3.5 m/s²), the margin depends on distance; the 1 s budget is kept.

findings.title: Stock PCS forwarding-loss budget has zero timing margin
findings.basis: Documentary finding; ISO normative verdict pending source verification
findings.analysis: The stated sum of detection and reaction equals FTTI before measured PCS timing. A watchdog nominal setting is insufficient to prove the end-to-end budget.
findings.action: Measure forwarding-loss response and PCS effects; include oscillator tolerance, scheduling, bus delay and safe-state behavior.
findings.closure: Worst-case FDTI+FRTI substantiated with positive justified margin or an explicitly accepted alternative safety argument.

evidence.excerpt: | OI-7 | SG-07 forwarding loss has zero margin (FDTI + FRTI = FTTI). Decide whether to shorten the watchdog and forwarding-supervision times below 0.1 s once the PCS timing is measured | Safety engineer | G2 |

findings.title: Freedom from interference is not established
findings.basis: Documentary finding; ISO normative verdict pending source verification
findings.analysis: The current verdicts include not shown and partially shown; the envelope-only ASIL allocation depends on resolving spatial, timing, communication and boot interference.
findings.action: Reconcile analysis to current pins, bound QM-triggered paths, document separation properties and verify adverse inputs and boot integrity.
findings.closure: Reviewed FFI/DFA with traceable evidence for every interference channel and justified ASIL allocation.

evidence.excerpt: | L-MCU spatial | Not shown | No MPU; QM-triggered paths execute in the same address space; SPI length unbounded (mitigated by memory-bank separation, unconfirmed) |

findings.title: The controlled Part 6 lifecycle has not been activated
findings.basis: Documentary finding; ISO normative verdict pending source verification
findings.analysis: The specification explicitly says entry prerequisites are draft/unapproved and Part 6 stays deferred. Existing code and host tests do not establish lifecycle completion.
findings.action: Close E-01…E-15 prerequisites and record the authorized lifecycle baseline and activation decision.
findings.closure: Approved entry checklist, input baselines, confirmation records and activation decision.

evidence.excerpt: Conclusion of the snapshot: no entry criterion is met. All the prerequisites exist as drafts, and the requirement chain from FSR to SWSR is populated and checked. None is approved or confirmed and no review record exists. Part 6 stays deferred, and the pre-entry track (§2.3) continues.

findings.title: HIL deferral prevents the stated verification closure
findings.basis: Documentary finding; ISO normative verdict pending source verification
findings.analysis: The safety plan records deferred HIL and says early-implementation credit cannot be earned until its conditions are met. Plans and host unit tests cannot replace target timing/fault-injection evidence.
findings.action: Resource a controlled target bench and execute baseline-bound campaigns; if deferred, keep associated gate claims explicitly open.
findings.closure: Target test logs, environment/calibration records, anomaly disposition and independent review.

evidence.excerpt: | OI-8 | Give a verification review at I1 or above to every at-risk envelope change in §4.1, and add their HIL campaign (REFERENCE_BUILD=1) to the bench plan. The lead answered on 2026-10-14: defer the HIL bench (DQ-049 option B), so condition (c) of §4.1 cannot be met until the bench is built | SM, VR | G2 |

findings.title: Tool self-tests and classification do not complete qualification
findings.basis: Documentary finding; ISO normative verdict pending source verification
findings.analysis: In-house safety-relevant tools have open TQR records and review work; compiler/runner pinning is also open. Agreement between tools sharing assumptions does not authenticate the standard.
findings.action: Complete TI/TD/TCL decisions and applicable qualification records; test error detection against independently sourced criteria and pin the toolchain.
findings.closure: Reviewed use-case-specific tool qualification, known limitations, detection evidence and immutable versions.

requirements.text: The envelope shall limit the commanded LKA torque magnitude to a speed-dependent bound derived from driver controllability (lateral acceleration and lateral deviation reached within the FTTI).
requirements.baseline_impl: Partial: fixed 1500 raw (`modes/toyota.h:173`); not speed-dependent, no physical rationale (GAP-04)

requirements.text: The envelope shall limit the rate of change of the commanded LKA torque (rise, fall and real-time window) to bounds derived from controllability.
requirements.baseline_impl: Implemented without rationale: 15/25 raw per frame, 450 raw per 250 ms (`modes/toyota.h:174-177`, `lateral.h:49-57, 87-95`) (GAP-04)

requirements.text: The envelope shall limit the commanded LKA torque to within a bounded difference of the measured EPS motor torque.
requirements.baseline_impl: Implemented: 350 raw (`modes/toyota.h:176`, `lateral.h:10-23`)

requirements.text: The envelope shall block any non-zero LKA torque or set steer-request bit while lateral authority is not granted.
requirements.baseline_impl: Implemented (`lateral.h:98-101`)

requirements.text: The envelope shall grant actuation authority only on a driver engagement action confirmed by the vehicle (rising edge of PCM cruise active) and shall revoke it when PCM cruise becomes inactive.
requirements.baseline_impl: Implemented (`safety.h:518-527`); PCM_CRUISE has no counter (GAP-01)

requirements.text: The envelope shall detect loss, corruption, repetition and staleness of each RX signal it uses for gating or limiting (PCM cruise state, brake, gas, driver/EPS torque, wheel speed) and revoke actuation authority within the FTTI allocation of §8.
requirements.baseline_impl: Partial: checksum on some messages, timeouts detected in ≤ ≈2 s (`safety.h:164-197, 321-344`); no counters, `0x226`/`0xAA` no checksum (`modes/toyota.h:40-46`) (GAP-01, GAP-06)

requirements.text: The envelope shall detect missing or stale control commands from the SoC and remove actuation within the FTTI allocation of §8.
requirements.baseline_impl: Partial: heartbeat mismatch 3 s, loss 5 s (`panda/board/main.c:182-213`); too slow for SG-01 (GAP-06); heartbeat shows pandad liveness only (GAP-10)

requirements.text: The envelope shall detect corruption, loss and reordering of command frames received from the SoC and discard affected frames.
requirements.baseline_impl: Partial: 8-bit XOR, no sequence counter (`panda/board/drivers/spi.h:97-138`, `can_comms.h:27`) (GAP-10)

requirements.text: The safety MCU shall detect its own execution faults (program-flow hang, clock failure, memory corruption, register corruption) and enter the safe state (no actuation TX, relay released) within the FTTI allocation of §8.
requirements.baseline_impl: Not implemented: IWDG never initialised (`panda/board/stm32h7/stm32h7_config.h:43`), software watchdog in same ISR (`main.c:301`), faults report-only, `PERMANENT_FAULTS = 0U` (`panda/board/sys/sys.h:50`) (GAP-07, GAP-08)

requirements.text: The safety mode and safety parameter for the reference configuration shall be fixed in the envelope and shall not be changeable by the SoC while a car safety mode is active; debug-only commands shall be unavailable in release builds; and the SoC shall not be able to make the safety MCU run non-release code or drive the relay outside the envelope through its reset and boot lines (GAP-38, refined by TSR-511).
requirements.baseline_impl: Not implemented: `0xdc` sets any mode at any time; `0xc5` relay drive not gated (`panda/board/main_comms.h:144-147, 222-225`) (GAP-09, GAP-25)

requirements.text: The envelope shall detect a harness relay malfunction (camera control messages seen on the car side) and inhibit all actuation TX.
requirements.baseline_impl: Implemented with 1–2 s grace and no contact readback (`safety.h:215-220, 372-380`) (GAP-12)

requirements.text: On any detected fault affecting lateral actuation, the envelope shall enter the lateral safe state (torque 0, steer request cleared) and keep it until a new valid engagement.
requirements.baseline_impl: Partial: violating frames dropped and `controls_allowed` cleared on RX faults (`lateral.h:141-148`, `safety.h:112-121`); a TX violation alone does not revoke authority

requirements.text: The EPS shall limit LKA torque to an overpowerable level and shall end LKA torque within a bounded time after `0x2E4` stops or carries the request bit cleared. (External measure, AOU-01R)
requirements.baseline_impl: Unverified (GAP-05)

requirements.text: The SoC controller shall command lateral motion with a margin below every envelope limit (target: commanded lateral acceleration ≤ 3.0 m/s², jerk ≤ 5 m/s³, torque ≤ 90 % of the envelope bound).
requirements.baseline_impl: Partial: 3.0 m/s², 5 m/s³ (`selfdrive/controls/lib/drive_helpers.py:9-14`); torque limits equal to envelope (`opendbc_repo/opendbc/car/toyota/values.py:20, 45-47`)

requirements.text: The item shall detect EPS conditions that remove or reduce LKA assistance (EPS LKA fault states) while engaged.
requirements.baseline_impl: Host-only (QM): `opendbc_repo/opendbc/car/toyota/carstate.py:122-127` → `steerTempUnavailable`/`steerUnavailable`; not in envelope (GAP-03)

requirements.text: The item shall detect loss of the inputs that the lateral command depends on (driving model output, calibration, localization, vehicle state) and shall not continue to actuate on inputs that are no longer valid.
requirements.allocated_to: E-01 (QM, see note), E-03 (FSR-01.07 as backstop)
requirements.baseline_impl: Not met: soft disable keeps actuating for 3 s on failed inputs (`selfdrive/selfdrived/state.py:7-8`); controlsd does not check freshness (`selfdrive/controls/controlsd.py:66, 122-127`) (GAP-16); diagnostics masked during big-model fallback (`selfdrive/selfdrived/selfdrived.py:382-384, 403, 457`) (GAP-17)

requirements.text: On a detected loss or degradation of lateral control, the item shall give a visual and acoustic take-over request within 1 s of fault detection and before or at the start of torque reduction.
requirements.allocated_to: E-01/HMI, E-03 siren for SoC loss
requirements.baseline_impl: Partial: soft/immediate disable alerts (`selfdrive/selfdrived/events.py:224-234`); timing not verified

requirements.text: When torque is withdrawn because of a fault (not a driver action), the reduction shall follow a bounded ramp unless the fault makes the command itself untrusted, in which case torque shall go to zero at once.
requirements.baseline_impl: Partial: rate-down limit 25 raw/frame enforced (`modes/toyota.h:175`); no defined fault ramp

requirements.text: On loss of communication with the SoC while engaged, the safety MCU shall give an acoustic warning that does not depend on the SoC.
requirements.baseline_impl: Partial: siren 3 s after heartbeat loss (`panda/board/main.c:193-205`); depends on 5 s detection (GAP-06). 2026-10-13: siren also at the 0.3 s heartbeat revocation (TSR-407) when authority was granted, ≈ 0.56 s after the last heartbeat, all builds (panda `c33343b`, TSR-516; WP-S-04 T-07a); not verified on hardware

requirements.text: Driver monitoring shall detect an inattentive or unresponsive driver while engaged and escalate warnings within the timing set in WP-C-08 (assurance/02-concept/WP-C-08-driver-hmi-misuse-analysis.md) §5.
requirements.baseline_impl: Implemented: 5/8/13 s vision, 5/15/25 s wheel-touch (`selfdrive/monitoring/policy.py:31-36`)

requirements.text: Driver monitoring shall detect its own invalidity (no driver image, camera blocked, model output missing or not credible) and fall back to a policy that is no less strict than the active policy.
requirements.baseline_impl: Partial: high-uncertainty → wheel-touch fallback (`policy.py:77-78`); source validity hard-coded `True` (`selfdrive/modeld/dmonitoringmodeld.py:99`); wheel-touch awareness reset by any steer/gas input (`policy.py:334-335`) (GAP-21)

requirements.text: Driver monitoring shall not be disabled, put into demo mode or replaced by synthetic inputs while the item can engage.
requirements.baseline_impl: Not met: `IsDriverViewEnabled` demo mode (`selfdrive/monitoring/dmonitoringd.py:26-27`, `policy.py:428-437`) (GAP-20)

requirements.text: If the driver does not respond to the highest DM warning, the item shall decelerate the vehicle, disengage and prevent re-engagement for a lockout period.
requirements.baseline_impl: Implemented: no-response force decel and lockout 1/5/15/30 min (`policy.py:39-44, 398`; `selfdrive/controls/controlsd.py:203-204`)

requirements.text: The item shall detect that the envelope does not grant actuation authority while the SoC is engaged (envelope blocking, stuck authority, safety-mode mismatch) and give a take-over request within the SG-02/SG-06 warning budget (§8).
requirements.baseline_impl: Partial: `controlsMismatch` raised after 200 frames ≈ 2 s (`selfdrive/selfdrived/selfdrived.py:338, 508-510`), longer than the ≤ 1 s budget. New in v0.2 (HE-02.4)

requirements.text: The item shall detect failure of the HMI path that shows the engagement state and gives take-over requests (display, sound) and treat it as a fault leading to disengagement with the SoC-independent indications (FSR-02.05 buzzer, FSR-05.05 cluster cruise state).
requirements.baseline_impl: Partial: a crashed `ui`/`soundd` raises `processNotRunning` (`selfdrive/selfdrived/selfdrived.py:351-357`); a hung but running UI, a frozen indication or muted audio is not detected. New in v0.2 (H-07, HE-07.x)

requirements.text: The envelope shall limit the commanded acceleration to an upper bound derived from controllability for the reference vehicle.
requirements.baseline_impl: Implemented without rationale: +2.0 m/s² (`modes/toyota.h:208`); `RAISED_ACCEL_LIMIT` not validated for Corolla (`opendbc_repo/opendbc/car/toyota/interface.py:117-118`) (GAP-04)

requirements.text: The envelope shall allow only the inactive acceleration value while longitudinal authority is not granted or while the driver presses the accelerator.
requirements.baseline_impl: Implemented (`longitudinal.h:3-12`)

requirements.text: The envelope shall limit the rate of increase of commanded acceleration (jerk).
requirements.baseline_impl: Not implemented (GAP-04)

requirements.text: FSR-01.05…01.12 apply to the longitudinal path (shared mechanisms; see trace §9).
requirements.baseline_impl: as referenced

requirements.text: On a detected fault affecting longitudinal control, the item shall stop requesting positive acceleration and request ACC cancel from the PCM.
requirements.baseline_impl: Partial: inactive value enforced; cancel bit set by host (`opendbc_repo/opendbc/car/toyota/carcontroller.py:253-254`)

requirements.text: The PCM shall bound ACC acceleration requests to its own envelope and honour the cancel request. (External measure, AOU-05R)
requirements.baseline_impl: Unverified (GAP-05)

requirements.text: The envelope shall limit the commanded deceleration to a bound derived from following-traffic controllability.
requirements.baseline_impl: Implemented without rationale: −3.5 m/s² (`modes/toyota.h:209`) (GAP-04)

requirements.text: The envelope shall limit the onset rate of commanded deceleration (negative jerk).
requirements.baseline_impl: Not implemented (GAP-04)

requirements.text: The transition to the longitudinal safe state shall not create a deceleration step larger than the jerk bound of FSR-04.02.
requirements.baseline_impl: Not specified; depends on PCM behaviour on inactive value (AOU-05R)

requirements.text: Driver accelerator input shall override commanded deceleration.
requirements.baseline_impl: Implemented in envelope (`longitudinal.h:3-5`); vehicle behaviour unverified

requirements.text: Deceleration that the item initiates for a reason other than following traffic (driver-monitoring no-response, fault soft disable) shall be preceded by a visual and acoustic alert and shall stay within the bounds of FSR-04.01/04.02.
requirements.baseline_impl: Partial: DM escalation alerts precede force deceleration (`selfdrive/monitoring/policy.py`); bounds as FSR-04.01, jerk not bounded (GAP-04). New in v0.2 (HE-04.3): DM is a source of H-04, and the deceleration path is bounded by the envelope, so DM itself stays QM (§7)

requirements.text: Forward collision warnings shall be raised only from valid, fresh inputs, and the false-warning rate in the ODD shall be bounded so that driver reflex braking with a close follower is not a credible consequence.
requirements.baseline_impl: Partial: FCW from model hard-brake prediction or planner (`selfdrive/selfdrived/selfdrived.py:440-445`); no false-rate target. **ASIL A on a QM element (E-01):** see OI-9. New in v0.2 (HE-04.5)

requirements.text: The envelope shall revoke all actuation authority on a driver brake press (rising edge, or pressed while moving) within the SG-05 FTTI.
requirements.baseline_impl: Implemented (`safety.h:354-356`); brake message `0x226` has no checksum or counter (GAP-01)

requirements.text: The envelope shall revoke all actuation authority when the PCM reports cruise inactive (cancel, main switch off).
requirements.baseline_impl: Implemented (`safety.h:520-521`)

requirements.text: The envelope shall detect driver steering override (driver torque above a threshold) and reduce the LKA torque so it does not oppose the driver.
requirements.baseline_impl: Not in envelope: host-only 500 raw check (`opendbc_repo/opendbc/car/toyota/carcontroller.py:33, 83`) (GAP-02)

requirements.text: The envelope shall block positive acceleration while the accelerator is pressed.
requirements.baseline_impl: Implemented (`longitudinal.h:3-5`)

requirements.text: The engagement state that the envelope enforces shall equal the PCM cruise state, so that the vehicle's own cruise indicator gives the driver an indication of engagement independent of the item's HMI.
requirements.baseline_impl: Implemented by FSR-01.05 design; independence of the cluster indication to be confirmed by test

requirements.text: If PCM cruise is active while the item is not engaged (or the reverse) for longer than a bounded time, the item shall warn the driver and request cancel.
requirements.baseline_impl: Not met: `cruiseMismatch` raised after 6 s with no reaction (`selfdrive/selfdrived/selfdrived.py:421`, `events.py:458-460`) (GAP-19)

requirements.text: Driver brake input shall produce braking regardless of ACC commands. (External measure, AOU-03R)
requirements.baseline_impl: Unverified

requirements.text: The item shall detect loss or staleness of the longitudinal plan, lead information (radar/vision) and model output while engaged.
requirements.baseline_impl: Partial: `commIssue`, `radarFault`, `processNotRunning` (`selfdrived.py:352-390`); masking during big-model settling (GAP-17); controlsd no freshness check (GAP-16)

requirements.text: On detected loss, the item shall give a take-over request within 1 s and cancel ACC so that control returns to the driver; it shall not hold a stale acceleration command.
requirements.baseline_impl: Partial: soft disable with force decel (`controlsd.py:203-204`, `selfdrive/controls/lib/longitudinal_planner.py:84-85`); stale inputs used for up to ≈3.5 s (GAP-16)

requirements.text: The item shall detect that the PCM does not execute ACC (ACC fault, cruise fault) and warn the driver.
requirements.baseline_impl: Implemented: `accFaulted` IMMEDIATE_DISABLE (`events.py:908`)

requirements.text: Non-finite or out-of-range actuator commands shall be treated as faults with a fault reaction, not silently replaced.
requirements.baseline_impl: Not met: silently clamped to 0 (`controlsd.py:140-147`) (GAP-19)

requirements.text: FSR-02.05 (independent acoustic warning on SoC loss) and FSR-02.06…02.09 (DM) also serve SG-06.
requirements.baseline_impl: as ref.

requirements.text: The item shall forward all camera-side messages to the car side unchanged, except the defined set of intercepted control messages.
requirements.baseline_impl: Implemented: static block list (`safety.h:270-281`)

requirements.text: The item shall not originate any message that the stock PCS function uses (e.g. PRE_COLLISION `0x344`, PCS_HUD `0x411`, AEB `0x283` with content) in the reference configuration.
requirements.baseline_impl: **Not met:** the openpilot-longitudinal TX whitelist allows the SoC to send `0x344` and `0x411` on bus 0 with no content check; only `0x283` is content-checked (`modes/toyota.h:19-28, 251-257`). The reference configuration host does not send them (`carcontroller.py:294-295` only with `DISABLE_RADAR`), but a QM fault could. (GAP-42)

requirements.text: On safety-MCU fault, loss of device power, or harness fault, the relay shall return to the stock camera-to-vehicle connection.
requirements.baseline_impl: Partial: SILENT/NO_OUTPUT release relay (`panda/board/main.c:45-54`); de-energised relay state and power-loss behaviour not confirmed (OI-6)

requirements.text: openpilot longitudinal commands shall not prevent PCS braking from taking priority in the PCM. (External measure, AOU-04R)
requirements.baseline_impl: Unverified

requirements.text: The item shall inform the driver when the stock system reports an AEB or FCW event.
requirements.baseline_impl: Implemented: `stockAeb`, `stockFcw` (`selfdrive/car/car_events.py:120-123`, `events.py:480`)

requirements.text: The safety MCU shall be supervised by a watchdog whose clock source and counter are independent of the CPU core clock tree and of the software it supervises, and whose expiry forces an MCU reset.
requirements.baseline_impl: **Implemented, not verified on hardware** (panda `9f60e17`: panda#1 and panda#3; impact record (assurance/07-supporting/impact/change-2026-10-12-panda-hw-watchdog.md)): IWDG1 (`IND_WDG`, `stm32h7/stm32h7_config.h:48`) on the LSI, prescaler /4, RLR 719, nominal timeout 90 ms at 32 kHz (`drivers/hw_watchdog.h`); expiry resets the MCU. The LSI tolerance and so the timeout at both ends are not yet confirmed from the datasheet (impact OI-2); HIL fault injection not run (impact OI-3, D-04). *As found before 2026-10-12: IWDG1 unused; only the software check of `drivers/simple_watchdog.h` from the 8 Hz tick, report-only (GAP-07).*

requirements.text: The watchdog shall be serviced only from a point that proves completion of the safety-relevant periodic processing (tick handler and RX/TX safety checks), not from an ISR that keeps running when the main processing has stalled.
requirements.baseline_impl: **Implemented, not verified on hardware** (panda `9f60e17`): fed only from the 100 Hz safety task (TIM4, `main.c:145`, after `safety_tick()` and the heartbeat check) and only when the main loop has run since the previous feed (`hw_watchdog_main_loop_alive()`, `main.c:124`), so a stall of the task interrupt or of the main loop ends in a reset. TX/RX hooks run in the CAN and host interrupts and are not themselves proven by the feed

requirements.text: The watchdog shall operate in window mode, so that servicing too early (runaway loop) is detected as well as servicing too late. Window and timeout shall be chosen so that detection plus reset completes within the MCU-execution-fault detection budget (≤ 0.1 s, set by the SG-07 FDTI, WP-S-04 §3.6).
requirements.baseline_impl: **Implemented, not verified on hardware** (panda `a35d1c6`, in pin `9f60e17`): WINR 679, so a feed is accepted only ≈ 5 ms or more after the previous one; timeout ≈ 90 ms nominal. The first tick after the start is skipped. ≤ 0.1 s holds only if the LSI is at most about 10 % slow (impact OI-2, open); HIL evidence open (OI-3)

requirements.text: The watchdog shall be started no later than the first time the harness relay is energised after a reset, on every path that energises it (by the application, the bootstub, or option-byte hardware start, if chosen), and shall then stay active in all modes until the next reset; it shall not be stoppable by the SoC. (Amended in v0.3 with TSR-501 v0.4.)
requirements.allocated_to: IWDG option bytes (IWDG_SW, freeze in stop/standby)
requirements.baseline_impl: **Implemented (software start), not verified on hardware:** `hw_watchdog_start()` is called from `set_intercept_relay()` the first time the relay is driven, on every path including `0xc5` (`drivers/harness.h:17-20`); once started it cannot be stopped by software. `enter_stop_mode()` resets the MCU first if the IWDG runs (`sys/power_saving.h:61-63`). Option-byte state (IWDG_SW, freeze in stop/standby) on shipped devices is not known (WP-H-02 (assurance/04-hardware/WP-H-02-hardware-design.md) UK-04, open)

requirements.text: An independent external supervisor (voltage supervisor with watchdog input, on its own clock) that can force the relay to its released state, independent of the MCU, should be added.
requirements.baseline_impl: Not present on the COTS PCB as far as observable. See WP-H-02 (assurance/04-hardware/WP-H-02-hardware-design.md) §6, DC-01. Needed for an ASIL C claim because IWDG shares supply and silicon with the CPU (GAP-11)

requirements.text: Every enabled interrupt shall have an explicitly configured NVIC priority, and a cycle counter independent of the interrupt load (Cortex-M7 DWT `CYCCNT`) shall be available to measure the execution time of the safety processing, so that the TSR-519 timing scheme can be configured and shown.
requirements.baseline_impl: Partial: explicit NVIC priority for every enabled interrupt (panda `52cad44`, `board/drivers/irq_priorities.h`); DWT present on the core, not used

requirements.text: In and after any MCU reset (power-on, brown-out, watchdog, software, external NRST from the SoC), the relay drive outputs shall be in the state that de-energises the intercept relay, and no CAN transceiver shall transmit actuation frames, until the firmware has re-established a valid safety mode.
requirements.parent_text: FSR-01.09, FSR-07.03 / TSR-502 (reset-state outputs), TSR-706 (relay to stock on reset)
requirements.allocated_to: GPIO reset state, relay driver circuit, transceiver standby pins
requirements.baseline_impl: **Partly observable.** Relay outputs are open-drain and written high (released) in `harness_init` (`drivers/harness.h:96-107`); the firmware starts in SILENT (`main.c:295`). GPIO reset state is analog/high-Z (`stm32h7_config.h:92-97`). Whether high-Z de-energises the relay depends on the driver circuit and pull-ups, which are **unknown without a schematic** (AOU-13, FSC OI-6)

requirements.text: The relay shall be de-energised (stock camera-to-vehicle path) when the device loses power or the harness 12 V supply is interrupted.
requirements.baseline_impl: Unverified (AOU-13)

requirements.text: Every unhandled exception (HardFault, NMI, MemManage, BusFault, UsageFault, unused vectors) and every fatal assertion shall end in a reset or in a state with relay released and CAN TX disabled; no fault path shall leave the MCU hung with the relay driven.
requirements.baseline_impl: **Partial.** NMI and HardFault set a cookie and reset (`early_init.h:66-80`). MemManage/BusFault/UsageFault are not enabled, so they escalate to HardFault (to confirm). Other vectors use `Default_Handler`, an infinite loop (`stm32h7/startup_stm32h7x5xx.s:111-114, 319-332`). `assert_fatal` hangs in `while(1)` (`libc.h:12-20`) and the clock init hangs on an unknown package or a non-starting HSE (`stm32h7/clock.h:68, 80`). Without an IWDG, a hang keeps the relay in its last state (GAP-07, GAP-08). *2026-10-12: once the relay has been driven, the IWDG (HWSR-501) now ends such a hang in a reset; not verified on hardware*

requirements.text: The SoC's control of the MCU reset (`STM_RST_N`) and boot-mode (`STM_BOOT0`) lines shall not be able to put the MCU into a state where the relay is driven by anything other than the release-signed application firmware.
requirements.allocated_to: Boot pins, option bytes (RDP/WRP), relay driver
requirements.baseline_impl: **Not met.** The SoC drives `STM_RST_N`/`STM_BOOT0` (`openpilot/common/hardware/comma/hardware.py:401-419`) (GAP-38). In the ROM bootloader the GPIOs are at reset state, so the relay is expected to be released (HWSR-502), which is the safe direction for SG-01/SG-07; the remaining risk is firmware substitution (cybersecurity, GAP-24)

requirements.text: The hardware ECC of all SRAM regions used by the safety firmware (DTCM, AXI SRAM, SRAM1/2, SRAM4, backup SRAM; `stm32h7/stm32h7x5_flash.ld:67-75`) shall be enabled, and uncorrectable (double-bit) errors shall be signalled to firmware and lead to the safe state.
requirements.baseline_impl: **Not implemented.** ECC on SRAM is a silicon feature (verify per RM0468); the RAMECC monitors and `ECC_IRQn` are not configured — `ECC_IRQHandler` only dispatches to the generic table (`stm32h7/interrupt_handlers.h:129`) and no handler is registered (GAP-08)

requirements.text: Single-bit (corrected) ECC error events shall be counted and reported in health, so that latent memory degradation is visible (latent-fault diagnostic).
requirements.baseline_impl: Not implemented

requirements.text: Flash ECC double-error detection shall lead to the safe state; single-error correction events shall be reported.
requirements.baseline_impl: Not handled (no reference to flash ECC flags in `stm32h7/llflash.h`)

requirements.text: The firmware image in flash shall be checked by a CRC (or hash) over the application region at start-up and periodically at run time, with a period no longer than the latent-fault interval used in WP-H-04 (proposed: once per drive cycle at start-up plus a background check completing at least once per hour of operation). A mismatch shall lead to the safe state.
requirements.baseline_impl: **Not implemented.** Only the bootstub signature check at boot (`bootstub.c:47-72`), which uses SHA-1/RSA-1024 and is not repeated at run time (GAP-24)

requirements.text: Critical configuration registers (clock, GPIO, FDCAN, relay pins) shall be checked periodically against their expected values, and divergence shall lead to the safe state rather than only a report.
requirements.baseline_impl: **Partial.** Register-divergence check runs at 1 Hz (`drivers/registers.h:56-70`, `main.c:229`) but only calls `fault_occurred()`; `PERMANENT_FAULTS` is `0U` (`sys/sys.h:50`) so no reaction (GAP-08)

requirements.text: Failure of the external high-speed oscillator (HSE, 25 MHz) shall be detected by the clock security system and lead to the safe state.
requirements.baseline_impl: **Implemented (detection).** CSS enabled (`stm32h7/clock.h:119`). On the STM32H7 a CSS event raises NMI (verify against RM0468); the NMI handler resets the MCU (`early_init.h:73-76`). After reset `clock_init` waits forever for `HSERDY` (`clock.h:80`) — a hang with GPIOs at reset state. Acceptable only if HWSR-502 is confirmed

requirements.text: Drift of the CPU/peripheral clock outside a tolerance that would invalidate timing-based checks (RX timeouts, heartbeat timeout, CAN bit timing) shall be detected by a cross-check against an independent clock (e.g. IWDG LSI or HSI vs HSE-derived timer).
requirements.baseline_impl: **Partial.** Interrupt-rate checks (`drivers/interrupts.h:34-37`) catch gross over-rates, report-only. No frequency cross-check

requirements.text: The MCU core and I/O supply shall be supervised so that operation below the specified minimum voltage is impossible (brown-out reset at a level inside the MCU's operating range).
requirements.baseline_impl: **Unknown.** BOR level is an option-byte setting; no code sets it. On-board supervisor unknown (schematic needed)

requirements.text: Supply degradation above the brown-out level but outside the safe operating range (programmable voltage detector) shall lead to the safe state before brown-out.
requirements.baseline_impl: **Not implemented.** `PVD_AVD_IRQHandler` exists only as a dispatch stub (`stm32h7/interrupt_handlers.h:7`); PVD is not enabled

requirements.text: The vehicle supply voltage at the device input shall be measured and reported; an out-of-range value while the relay is driven shall lead to the safe state. Thresholds to be set from the device input rating.
requirements.baseline_impl: **Partial.** Measured and reported only: `cuatro_read_voltage_mV` (ADC1 ch8 ×11, `boards/cuatro.h:28-30`), `red_read_voltage_mV` used by tres (ADC1 ch2 ×11, `boards/red.h:70-72`, `boards/tres.h:162`), reported in health (`main_comms.h:14`). Host uses it only for power management (`openpilot/system/hardware/power_monitoring.py`)

requirements.text: The Cortex-M7 MPU shall be configured so that safety-critical data (safety mode, limits, `controls_allowed`, relay state) and the stack are protected against writes from non-safety code paths (USB/SPI comms handlers), stack overflow is trapped by a guard region, and code regions are non-writable; MemManage faults shall lead to the safe state.
requirements.baseline_impl: **Not implemented.** No MPU configuration in `panda/board` (`mpu_armv7.h` is vendored in `stm32h7/inc/` but unused) (GAP-08, GAP-11)

requirements.text: The intercept relay shall be energised only by an active output from the MCU (de-energise-to-safe): any open circuit, MCU reset or loss of drive shall release it.
requirements.baseline_impl: Relay outputs are open-drain, active-low (`drivers/harness.h:22-28, 98-101`); "released" = output high/open. Driver circuit unknown (AOU-13)

requirements.text: The actual relay contact state (or the continuity of the camera-to-car path) shall be read back by the MCU independently of the drive signal, and a mismatch between commanded and actual state shall be detected within the SG-01 detection budget (≤ 0.3 s) in both directions (stuck released and stuck intercepting).
requirements.allocated_to: Relay auxiliary contact or bus-sense circuit
requirements.baseline_impl: **Not implemented (GAP-12).** Current detection is indirect and one-directional: camera control messages seen on the car side after a 1 s transition timeout (`safety.h:372-380`), checked at 1 Hz in `safety_tick` (so 1–2 s). "Stuck intercepting while commanded released" is not detected at all

requirements.text: A detected relay malfunction shall inhibit all actuation TX until the next power cycle, and shall be reported to the SoC.
requirements.baseline_impl: **Implemented.** `relay_malfunction` blocks TX (`safety.h:252`) and forwarding (`safety.h:268`); reported as `FAULT_RELAY_MALFUNCTION` (`main.c:122-129`); host immediate-disable (`openpilot/selfdrive/selfdrived/selfdrived.py:341`). Cleared on any safety-mode change (`safety.h:427, 459`), not latched to a power cycle

requirements.text: The relay drive path shall not be operable by debug commands in release builds.
requirements.baseline_impl: **Partial.** In the reference build (`LIONDRIVER_REFERENCE=1`) `0xc5` is refused in a car mode (`reference_lock.h`, panda `9f60e17`); it is still operable in SILENT/NOOUTPUT, and in other builds it drives the relay without `ALLOW_DEBUG` gating (`main_comms.h:164-166`) (GAP-09). Not verified on hardware

requirements.text: The relay's rated contact life, switching current and coil characteristics shall cover the expected number of engage/release cycles over the vehicle life with margin.
requirements.baseline_impl: Part number unknown (WP-H-07 (assurance/04-hardware/WP-H-07-hardware-component-qualification.md) QE-05)

requirements.text: The CAN transceivers on the actuation bus (car side) shall be in a non-transmitting state from reset until the firmware enables them, and the firmware shall be able to disable them as part of the safe state.
requirements.baseline_impl: Enable lines are active-low GPIOs per transceiver (`boards/cuatro.h:9-26`; `boards/tres.h:32-56`); enabled after SILENT is set (`main.c:295-298`). Behaviour of the enable pin at high-Z (MCU reset) depends on board pull-ups — unknown

requirements.text: A transceiver failure that produces a dominant-stuck or babbling bus shall not prevent the stock camera-to-vehicle path from working once the relay is released.
requirements.baseline_impl: Unknown: depends on whether the panda transceivers stay attached to the car-side bus when the relay is released

requirements.text: Bus-off, error-passive and persistent TX failure on the car-side bus while engaged shall be detected and lead to the actuation safe state and a driver warning.
requirements.baseline_impl: **Partial.** Bus-off and error counters read into `can_health` (`drivers/fdcan.h:44-63`); on bus-off the core is reset (`drivers/fdcan.h:76-84`, `can_clear_send` rate-limited to 10 Hz, `:23-34`). No safety reaction in firmware; the host raises `canError` (gap assessment GAP-19 for wrong text)

requirements.text: CAN controller interrupt storms shall be detected and lead to the safe state.
requirements.baseline_impl: Detected, report-only (`drivers/fdcan.h:257-262`, `drivers/interrupts.h:34-37`) (GAP-08)

requirements.text: The MCU shall be able to receive the actuation frames it transmits on the car-side bus as they appear on the bus (for example through a second FDCAN instance or the transceiver's receive line on that bus), so that the read-back of TSR-517 covers FDCAN message RAM, FDCAN core and transceiver and not only the internal TX path.
requirements.allocated_to: Car-side FDCAN instance, transceiver RX path
requirements.baseline_impl: Unknown: whether own frames can be received from the bus on this board is to be shown in WP-H-02 (the FDCAN TX event FIFO reflects internal state only)

requirements.text: The ignition state shall be sensed from the harness ignition line; loss or implausibility of the ignition signal shall not leave the relay driven without a valid heartbeat.
requirements.allocated_to: Harness SBU ignition line, MCU input
requirements.baseline_impl: **Partial.** `harness_check_ignition` reads the SBU line selected by orientation (`drivers/harness.h:35-52`). Toyota has no CAN ignition hook (`opendbc_repo/opendbc/safety/ignition.h:12-63` covers GM, Rivian, Tesla, Mazda, VW MEB only), so the Corolla relies on the line alone. Ignition sets the heartbeat timeout: 5 s with ignition, 2 s without (`main.c:101-103, 193`)

requirements.text: A short or open of the ignition line shall be detected or shown to be safe (an open line reads "ignition off" and shortens the heartbeat timeout — safe direction; a short to ground reads "ignition on" — longer timeout, analyse).
requirements.baseline_impl: Not analysed (WP-H-03 (assurance/04-hardware/WP-H-03-hardware-safety-analysis-fmeda.md) FM-IGN-*)

requirements.text: The safety MCU die temperature shall be monitored, and operation outside the MCU's specified junction range shall lead to the safe state.
requirements.baseline_impl: **Partial.** DTS read and reported (`stm32h7/lldts.h`, `main_comms.h:51-52`), no reaction in firmware. The host's thermal policy uses SoC CPU/GPU/memory/PMIC temperatures only, not the panda DTS (`openpilot/system/hardware/hardwared.py:320-329`)

requirements.text: Loss of forced cooling (fan stall) shall be detected.
requirements.asil: QM (availability) / B if thermal margin requires it
requirements.baseline_impl: Tach measured (`drivers/fan.h:23-43`); host raises a fault when fan < 500 rpm for > 15 s (onboard review, `selfdrived.py:268-271`)

requirements.text: The SPI link shall carry an integrity mechanism strong enough for the residual-error target of the TSR (e.g. CRC-16 or stronger plus a sequence counter); the HW part is the SPI peripheral and DMA, which shall report overrun and mode faults.
requirements.baseline_impl: Weak: 8-bit XOR (`drivers/spi.h:97-104`) (GAP-10). Software requirement; listed here for the HSI

requirements.text: The harness orientation (normal, flipped, not connected) shall be detected before the relay is driven, and the CAN routing and relay/ignition pin assignment shall follow the detected orientation.
requirements.baseline_impl: **Implemented.** ADC of SBU1/SBU2 against `avdd_mV/2` (`drivers/harness.h:54-90`); relay/ignition pin swap by orientation (`drivers/harness.h:22-28`); CAN pin mux by orientation (`boards/tres.h:58-98`). Detection is skipped while the relay is driven (`drivers/harness.h:59`)

requirements.text: A change of detected orientation or loss of harness while the relay is driven shall be detected and lead to the safe state.
requirements.baseline_impl: Partial: orientation change re-inits CAN and the safety mode (`main.c:132-140`), but detection is suspended while the relay is driven, so harness disconnection is seen only through CAN/heartbeat effects

requirements.text: In the de-energised relay state the harness shall connect the forward camera to the vehicle CAN without any active component in the path (stock PCS path).
requirements.baseline_impl: Unverified (AOU-13, FSC OI-6). Code comment "keep buses connected by default" (`drivers/harness.h:106`) supports this but is not evidence

requirements.text: Harness connectors shall be keyed/latched so that partial insertion is detected (NC status) or cannot occur.
requirements.baseline_impl: Unknown

requirements.text: The camera-side FDCAN controller's error state (error-passive, bus-off) and its reception activity shall be observable by the firmware, so that a loss of camera-side forwarding can be detected within the SG-07 FDTI (≤ 0.1 s).
requirements.baseline_impl: Partial: FDCAN error counters and bus-off status are read (`drivers/fdcan.h:76-84`); no supervision acts on them for the camera side

requirements.text: From the moment the relay drive is released, the intercept relay shall restore the stock camera-to-vehicle path within ≤ 20 ms (drop-out time including contact bounce), so that the relay part of the SG-07 FRTI (≤ 0.1 s) holds with margin.
requirements.baseline_impl: Part number unknown (WP-H-02); assumption A-PCS-2 of WP-S-04 §3.6

requirements.text: The siren path (MCU output, codec or amplifier, speaker) shall produce the warning when commanded by the MCU with the SoC hung or powered down, and shall not depend on any part that the SoC can disable.
requirements.allocated_to: DAC/DMA and codec over I2C5 (tres) or SAI4 amplifier (cuatro); speaker
requirements.baseline_impl: Unknown: whether codec, amplifier and speaker are shared with SoC audio (WP-H-02 HE-17; WP-A-03 DFI-23)

requirements.text: The siren shall be audible at the driver's position over cabin noise at the highest ODD speed; the sound level shall be set in WP-C-08.
requirements.baseline_impl: Not assessed

requirements.text: A failure of the siren path (codec not responding, amplifier fault) shall be detectable by the firmware at start-up (TSR-515).
requirements.allocated_to: Codec I2C acknowledge or amplifier fault output
requirements.baseline_impl: Partial: codec I2C failure reported only (`drivers/fake_siren.h:38-52`)

requirements.text: The Toyota TX hook shall reject every STEERING_LKA (`0x2E4`, bus 0) frame whose decoded STEER_TORQUE_CMD magnitude exceeds τ_max, where τ_max is 1500 raw until SWSR-102 is implemented.
requirements.acceptance: \|τ\| = τ_max accepted, τ_max + 1 rejected, both signs, extreme int16 rejected
requirements.baseline_impl: Impl: `modes/toyota.h:173`, check `lateral.h:73-74`. No physical rationale (GAP-04)

requirements.text: The Toyota TX hook shall decode `0x2E4` as STEER_REQUEST = bit 0 and STEER_TORQUE_CMD = signed 16-bit from data bytes 1–2 (big-endian), and shall evaluate it only for frames on bus 0 with length 5.
requirements.acceptance: Decoding matches the DBC for all 2^16 torque values; other lengths not whitelisted
requirements.baseline_impl: Impl: `modes/toyota.h:11, 322-325`; length match `helpers.h:60-64`

requirements.text: When a speed-dependent bound is configured, the lateral check shall use τ_max(v) from the calibration table CD-22 and the speed value that yields the smaller bound under speed uncertainty.
requirements.acceptance: Bound at every breakpoint and midpoint equals the table; uncertainty direction verified against the table shape
requirements.baseline_impl: Not impl: `dynamic_max_torque` unset for Toyota (`modes/toyota.h:172-186`); mechanism `lateral.h:66-71` uses `vehicle_speed.min − 1 m/s`, conservative only for increasing tables; `struct lookup_t` holds 3 breakpoints only (`declarations.h`) (GAP-04, WP-S-02 OI-3)

requirements.text: The τ_max(v) table shall be checked at build time for monotonic speed breakpoints and values within [0, 1500] raw; a failed check shall fail the build.
requirements.acceptance: Build fails on a non-monotonic or out-of-range table
requirements.baseline_impl: Not impl; WP-W-09 (assurance/05-software/WP-W-09-configuration-calibration-data.md) DVR-22

requirements.text: The lateral check shall reject a `0x2E4` frame whose torque magnitude increases by more than Δ_up = 15 raw, or decreases by more than Δ_down = 25 raw, relative to the last accepted torque.
requirements.acceptance: Violation exactly at Δ + 1 raw for up and down, both signs
requirements.baseline_impl: Impl: `modes/toyota.h:174-175`; `lateral.h:14-19` (inside `dist_to_meas_check`). Values without rationale (GAP-04)

requirements.text: The lateral check shall reject a `0x2E4` frame whose torque differs by more than 450 raw from the reference torque stored at the start of the current 250 ms window, and shall restart the window after 250 ms.
requirements.acceptance: Rejection at 451 raw; window restart at 250 ms with timer resolution 1 µs
requirements.baseline_impl: Impl: `modes/toyota.h:177`; `lateral.h:49-57, 87-95`; `MAX_RT_INTERVAL` `declarations.h:71`

requirements.text: The lateral check shall reject a `0x2E4` frame whose torque exceeds the maximum (or is below the minimum) of the last 6 scaled EPS motor-torque samples widened by 1 raw by more than Δ_meas = 350 raw, with the downward-rate exception of the baseline algorithm.
requirements.acceptance: Rejection at meas.max + 1 + 351 raw; window of exactly 6 samples
requirements.baseline_impl: Impl: `modes/toyota.h:98-111, 176`; `lateral.h:10-23, 82-83`; `MAX_SAMPLE_VALS` `declarations.h:68`

requirements.text: The EPS torque scale factor used by SWSR-104 shall be the reference value 73 compiled into the firmware; a safety parameter carrying a different factor shall be rejected per SWSR-512.
requirements.acceptance: Only `param & 0xFF == 73` accepted in the reference build
requirements.applies_to: CFG-001, reference build only (`LIONDRIVER_REFERENCE=1`); other builds keep the upstream behaviour
requirements.baseline_impl: Met in the reference build through the panda lock, not verified on hardware: TOYOTA is accepted only with parameter 73 (panda `8aa8671`, `board/reference_lock.h`, SWSR-512). `toyota_init` itself has no range check and accepts any factor 0–255 (opendbc `7993399`, `modes/toyota.h:492`), so builds without `LIONDRIVER_REFERENCE` still do (GAP-44, GAP-09)

requirements.text: While lateral authority is not granted, the lateral check shall reject every `0x2E4` frame with non-zero torque or with STEER_REQUEST = 1.
requirements.acceptance: All four combinations of (torque≠0, request) rejected except (0, 0)
requirements.baseline_impl: Partial: non-zero torque rejected (`lateral.h:98-101`); request = 1 with zero torque accepted (`lateral.h:105`) (GAP-48)

requirements.text: While authority is granted, the lateral check shall accept STEER_REQUEST = 0 with non-zero torque for at most 1 consecutive frame, only after ≥ 17 consecutive valid frames and ≥ 162 ms after the previous such frame.
requirements.acceptance: Boundary at 16/17 frames, 2 consecutive cuts, 161/162 ms
requirements.baseline_impl: Impl: `modes/toyota.h:182-185`; `lateral.h:111-138`

requirements.text: In the LKA configuration the Toyota TX hook shall reject any STEERING_LTA (`0x191`) frame with STEER_REQUEST, STEER_REQUEST_2, a non-zero angle command or a non-zero TORQUE_WIND_DOWN.
requirements.acceptance: Each field set alone → rejected
requirements.baseline_impl: Impl: `modes/toyota.h:260-273`

requirements.text: If a `0x2E4` frame is rejected while lateral authority is granted, the envelope shall clear lateral authority in the same call and keep it cleared until the next valid engagement per SWSR-301.
requirements.acceptance: `controls_allowed` false after the first violating frame; no frame accepted until a new PCM rising edge
requirements.baseline_impl: Not impl: frame dropped and limiter state reset (`lateral.h:140-148`), `controls_allowed` unchanged (WP-S-02 OI-4)

requirements.text: The envelope shall record the cause of every authority revocation as a reason code (at least: TX violation, RX checksum, RX timeout, RX plausibility, brake, cruise off, heartbeat, command stall, platform fault) and report the latest code and a per-cause counter in the health packet.
requirements.acceptance: Each cause produces its distinct code in `0xd2` health within one health period
requirements.baseline_impl: Partial: no general reason code yet (OI-8). Reported today: `safety_tx_blocked` count and the RX-invalid flag (`main_comms.h`); in addition since 2026-10-12 the health flags EPS fault (bit 10, `pandaState.epsFault`), TX rate exceeded (bit 11, `pandaState.txRateExceeded`) and watchdog reset (bit 9, `pandaState.watchdogReset`), and the refused-request counter `requests_rejected_pkt` (panda `8aa8671`, `board/health.h`); interface change in WP-S-05 §4.2 (assurance/03-system/WP-S-05-hsi-specification.md)

requirements.text: When the envelope rejects a `0x2E4` frame, it shall transmit in its place a `0x2E4` frame with torque 0, STEER_REQUEST 0, the message counter continuing the SoC sequence and a valid Toyota checksum.
requirements.acceptance: Substitute frame on bus 0 within one frame period of the rejected frame; EPS torque at zero ≤ 0.1 s (VT, WP-S-04 M-02)
requirements.baseline_impl: Not impl: rejected frame is only counted and returned to the SoC (`drivers/can_common.h:161-176`) (GAP-46)

requirements.text: After lateral authority is revoked for a reason that stops SoC frames (heartbeat loss, command stall, platform fault), the envelope shall transmit zero-torque `0x2E4` frames autonomously at 100 Hz until the EPS reports LKA inactive or for 1 s, whichever is earlier, unless the relay is released.
requirements.acceptance: Zero frames present on bus 0 from ≤ 10 ms after revocation
requirements.baseline_impl: Not impl; needs the periodic task of SWSR-401a and a design decision on frame ownership (OI-3)

requirements.text: The Toyota RX configuration shall include EPS_STATUS (`0x262`) with checksum and timeout supervision, and while lateral authority is granted the envelope shall revoke it when LKA_STATE is in the confirmed fault set or `0x262` times out.
requirements.acceptance: Revocation within 1 frame of a fault code; fault set confirmed on reference EPS logs
requirements.baseline_impl: Partial (reference build): `0x262` in the RX set with checksum and timeout (opendbc `98404a4`, test `test_reference_rx_checks`); lateral actuation refused while LKA_STATE is in the host's fault set (opendbc `242d63d`; `toyota_lka_state_is_fault`, `modes/toyota.h`; test `test_eps_fault_blocks_lka`, every code 0…127). The frame that reports the fault removes authority for the next STEERING_LKA frame. The state is reported to the host (`safety_eps_fault` → health flag bit 10 → `pandaState.epsFault`; panda `877730e`, opendbc `adcb7c2`; HIL test `tests/hitl/test_13_eps_fault.py`, not run). Open: fault set confirmed on reference EPS logs (verification criterion) (GAP-03)

requirements.text: The Toyota TX hook shall reject every ACC_CONTROL (`0x343`, bus 0) frame whose ACCEL_CMD exceeds a_max = 2000 raw (+2.0 m/s²).
requirements.acceptance: 2000 accepted, 2001 rejected
requirements.baseline_impl: Impl: `modes/toyota.h:207-210, 225`; `longitudinal.h:8-12` (GAP-04)

requirements.text: The Toyota TX hook shall decode ACCEL_CMD as signed 16-bit from data bytes 0–1 (big-endian, 0.001 m/s² per raw).
requirements.acceptance: Decoding matches DBC over full range
requirements.baseline_impl: Impl: `modes/toyota.h:217-218`

requirements.text: The Toyota TX hook shall reject every `0x343` frame whose ACCEL_CMD is below a_min = −3500 raw (−3.5 m/s²).
requirements.acceptance: −3500 accepted, −3501 rejected
requirements.baseline_impl: Impl: `modes/toyota.h:209`

requirements.text: While longitudinal authority is not granted (not engaged, or gas pressed in the previous RX frame), the TX hook shall accept `0x343` only with ACCEL_CMD equal to the inactive value 0, defined as a named constant.
requirements.acceptance: Any non-zero value rejected in each non-granted state
requirements.baseline_impl: Impl: `longitudinal.h:3-12`; inactive value is the implicit zero-initialised field of `TOYOTA_LONG_LIMITS` (`modes/toyota.h:207-210`) — make explicit (G-01)

requirements.text: The TX hook shall reject a `0x343` frame whose ACCEL_CMD increases relative to the last accepted value faster than j_up (raw per frame; 0 m/s² taken as last value at engagement).
requirements.acceptance: Rejection at j_up + 1 raw per frame
requirements.baseline_impl: Not impl (GAP-04); host wind-up only (`carcontroller.py:21`)

requirements.text: The TX hook shall reject a `0x343` frame whose ACCEL_CMD decreases faster than j_down.
requirements.acceptance: Rejection at j_down + 1 raw per frame
requirements.baseline_impl: Not impl (GAP-04); host only (`carcontroller.py:22`)

requirements.text: If vehicle characterisation does not show a bounded PCM response to a step to the inactive value, the TX hook shall, for at most 1 s after revocation, accept `0x343` values that move monotonically towards 0 at no more than j_down/j_up.
requirements.acceptance: Wind-down accepted, any increase in magnitude rejected, all non-zero rejected after 1 s
requirements.baseline_impl: Not impl; decision depends on WP-S-04 M-03 (AOU-05R)

requirements.text: The TX hook shall check PERMIT_BRAKING, CANCEL_REQ, RELEASE_STANDSTILL and ACCEL_CMD_ALT of `0x343` against the values allowed in the current authority state; without authority, only frames that request no acceleration, no braking and no standstill release shall pass.
requirements.acceptance: Each field set alone without authority → rejected
requirements.baseline_impl: Partial: only ACCEL_CMD checked (`modes/toyota.h:216-241`) (GAP-48)

requirements.text: The envelope shall set authority only on a rising edge of PCM_CRUISE (`0x1D2`) CRUISE_ACTIVE (bit 5) and clear it in the RX call in which CRUISE_ACTIVE = 0 is received.
requirements.acceptance: State table of WP-W-05 §5.2 fully covered
requirements.baseline_impl: Impl: `safety.h:518-527`; `modes/toyota.h:143-146`

requirements.text: The envelope shall clear authority when BRAKE_PRESSED (`0x226` bit 37) rises, or is set while any wheel speed is non-zero.
requirements.acceptance: Clear in the same RX call
requirements.baseline_impl: Impl: `safety.h:350-357`; `modes/toyota.h:148-150, 157-168`. `0x226` without checksum (GAP-01) → SWSR-405

requirements.text: `controlsd` and the Toyota carcontroller shall set CANCEL_REQ in ACC_CONTROL on every fault-induced disengagement while PCM cruise is on, with or without openpilot longitudinal.
requirements.acceptance: CANCEL_REQ = 1 within 0.1 s of disengagement, in both longitudinal modes
requirements.baseline_impl: Impl: `controlsd.py:162`; `carcontroller.py:253-254, 269-273`

requirements.text: The lateral check shall reject `0x2E4` frames that increase torque opposing a driver torque beyond the driver allowance, using the last 6 STEER_TORQUE_DRIVER samples of `0x260`.
requirements.acceptance: Boundary at allowance ± 1 raw
requirements.baseline_impl: Not impl on LKA path: Toyota uses `TorqueMotorLimited` (`modes/toyota.h:178`); driver samples used for LTA only (`:113-116, 294-298`); `driver_limit_check` exists (`lateral.h:26-46`) (GAP-02)

requirements.text: When \|driver torque\| exceeds T_ovr for longer than t_ovr while lateral authority is granted, the envelope shall clear lateral authority (via `steering_disengage`).
requirements.acceptance: Clear at t_ovr + 1 frame; values from WP-C-08
requirements.baseline_impl: Not impl: `steering_disengage` edge handling exists (`safety.h:365-369`), not set by Toyota (GAP-02)

requirements.text: While GAS_RELEASED (`0x1D2` bit 4) = 0 the envelope shall treat longitudinal authority as not granted and shall not clear lateral authority.
requirements.acceptance: Lateral accepted, `0x343` non-inactive rejected while gas pressed
requirements.baseline_impl: Impl: `modes/toyota.h:146`; `longitudinal.h:3-5`

requirements.text: The envelope shall not set authority on a PCM rising edge while any RX check (checksum, timeout, rate, frozen, cross-check, quality) of the configured RX set is failed or has not yet been evaluated since its last frame.
requirements.acceptance: Rising edge ignored while any message lags > 5 periods
requirements.baseline_impl: Partial (opendbc `aff4033`): rising edge gated on seen, checksum, counter, quality and timeout for Toyota (`rx_checks_allow_engagement()`); frozen-value and cross-checks do not exist yet (IA RX timeout (assurance/07-supporting/impact/change-2026-10-12-opendbc-toyota-rx-timeout.md) §7)

requirements.text: When authority is granted and the SoC heartbeat reports "not engaged" for > 0.3 s, the envelope shall clear authority.
requirements.acceptance: Clear within 0.3 s + one task period
requirements.baseline_impl: Not met: 3 consecutive 1 Hz ticks (`main.c:181-189`) (GAP-06)

requirements.text: `selfdrived` shall immediately disable when the panda-reported authority differs from its engaged state for > 0.3 s.
requirements.acceptance: Event within 30 frames
requirements.baseline_impl: Not met: 200 frames (`selfdrive/selfdrived/selfdrived.py:338, 503-510`)

requirements.text: If PCM cruise is active while not engaged, or engaged while PCM cruise is inactive, for > 1 s, `selfdrived` shall warn and `card` shall request ACC cancel.
requirements.acceptance: Warning and cancel within 1 s
requirements.baseline_impl: Implemented: 1 s, repeating prompt; cancel requested by `controlsd` (`selfdrived.py`, `events.py`)

requirements.text: `controls_allowed` shall be set true only by the PCM rising-edge logic of SWSR-301; no comms handler, heartbeat or mode-setting path shall set it true.
requirements.acceptance: Code inspection: single write of `true`
requirements.baseline_impl: Impl: only write of `true` is `safety.h:524` (in E-03 code; test harness excepted)

requirements.text: Authority shall be false and all limiter, sample and edge state reset at MCU start-up and on every safety-mode change. The CRUISE_ACTIVE edge state shall reset to "not yet seen disengaged": after the change, authority shall be granted only on a rising edge that follows the reception of CRUISE_ACTIVE = 0 (SWSR-301).
requirements.acceptance: All state variables of WP-W-05 §5.1 at reset values after `set_safety_hooks`
requirements.baseline_impl: Impl: `safety.h:57, 425-460`. Edge state "not yet seen disengaged" (amendment, ATC-26): not at the pinned opendbc; proposed change change-2026-10-14-mode-set-regrant (assurance/07-supporting/impact/change-2026-10-14-mode-set-regrant.md)

requirements.text: For every message in the Toyota RX check set, the envelope shall flag a timeout when no frame was received for more than 5 nominal periods, and shall clear authority on the flag.
requirements.acceptance: Detection ≤ 5 periods + one task period (≤ 0.2 s for 33 Hz `0x1D2`)
requirements.baseline_impl: Met for the Toyota RX checks: the four common ones (opendbc `aff4033`) and, in the reference build, `0x262` and `0x1D3` (opendbc `98404a4`); `safety.h` `rx_check_lagging()`, `modes/toyota.h`; `0xB4` not added (no nominal rate); not yet verified on hardware (IA RX timeout (assurance/07-supporting/impact/change-2026-10-12-opendbc-toyota-rx-timeout.md))

requirements.text: The RX timeout evaluation (and the other periodic checks of SWSR-307, 403, 404, 405, 407, 408, 413, 506) shall run in a periodic safety task at ≥ 50 Hz on a timer interrupt separate from the comms interrupts.
requirements.acceptance: Measured period ≤ 20 ms, jitter recorded
requirements.baseline_impl: Partial (panda `9f60e17`): TIM4 100 Hz safety task runs `safety_tick()` (RX timeout), the heartbeat monitor (SWSR-407) and feeds the IWDG; the checks of SWSR-307, 403, 404, 405, 408, 413 and 506 do not run in it (`main.c` `safety_task_handler`), rate fault at 110 Hz. Period and jitter not yet measured (IA watchdog (assurance/07-supporting/impact/change-2026-10-12-panda-hw-watchdog.md) §7)

requirements.text: The envelope shall verify the Toyota additive checksum and length of `0x260` and `0x1D2` (and `0x262`, `0x1D3`, which are in the reference-build RX set since opendbc `98404a4`; `0xB4` once added) on every frame and treat one failure as an RX fault.
requirements.acceptance: Single bit flip in data or checksum → fault
requirements.baseline_impl: Impl: `safety.h:164-197`; `modes/toyota.h:40-46, 65-77`; 8-bit additive (GAP-01)

requirements.text: The envelope shall flag an RX fault when a configured message arrives at more than 1.5× its nominal rate over a 100 ms window.
requirements.acceptance: Fault at injected 1.5× + 1 frame per window; no fault on reference logs (RP)
requirements.baseline_impl: Not impl (GAP-01)

requirements.text: The envelope shall flag an RX fault when the data field (excluding checksum) of `0x260` torque/angle bytes, of `0xAA` (vehicle moving above v_min) or of `0xB4` ENCODER stays identical for longer than t_frz.
requirements.acceptance: Detection ≤ t_frz; no false detection on the reference log set
requirements.baseline_impl: Not impl (GAP-01)

requirements.text: The envelope shall flag an RX fault when (a) mean wheel speed from `0xAA` and SPEED from `0xB4` differ by > 2 m/s, (b) BRAKE_PRESSED in `0x226` and in `0x1D3` disagree (the envelope then treats the brake as pressed), (c) CRUISE_ACTIVE = 1 with `0x1D3` MAIN_ON = 0, or (d) with authority granted, measured EPS torque does not follow the accepted command within the EPS-response tolerance, each for longer than its tolerance time. For (c), CRUISE_ACTIVE changing to 1 while MAIN_ON = 0 shall be an RX fault at once, without tolerance.
requirements.acceptance: Each disagreement detected ≤ 0.2 s; no false detection on reference logs
requirements.baseline_impl: Partial (reference build, opendbc `875e325`): (c) implemented (`toyota_cruise_main_check`, `modes/toyota.h`; test `test_cruise_active_with_main_off`; tolerance 150 ms). Not impl: (a) (`speed_mismatch_check` exists, unused, `safety.h:529-537`); (b) pending the `0x1D3` BRAKE_PRESSED semantics on reference logs; (d) (GAP-01)

requirements.text: On any RX fault the envelope shall clear all authority in the same call, report the reason (SWSR-108a), and not set authority again until all RX checks pass and a new PCM rising edge occurs.
requirements.acceptance: Reaction in same call; re-engage only after edge
requirements.baseline_impl: Partial: `safety.h:112-121, 337-340`; single flag `main_comms.h:23`

requirements.text: In a car safety mode the envelope shall clear all authority when no heartbeat (`0xf3`) has been received for > 0.3 s.
requirements.acceptance: Clear ≤ 0.3 s + one task period
requirements.baseline_impl: Implemented (panda `c2e5d93`, `drivers/heartbeat_monitor.h`); host tests `tests/heartbeat_monitor`; not yet verified on hardware (IA heartbeat (assurance/07-supporting/impact/change-2026-10-12-panda-fast-heartbeat.md)). TSR-407 is Partial because its SS-S part (SILENT after the TSR-510 timeout, SWSR-510) is still 5 s; the revocation this SWSR covers is implemented

requirements.text: While lateral authority is granted, the envelope shall clear authority when no `0x2E4` frame has been accepted for > 50 ms; while longitudinal authority is granted, the same for `0x343` with > 100 ms.
requirements.acceptance: Clear at 50/100 ms + task period; SS-L via SWSR-109a
requirements.baseline_impl: Impl in the reference build (opendbc `273f44e`): `tx_arrival_checks` (`safety.h`), Toyota table (`modes/toyota.h`); unit tests `test_tx_arrival_*`; HIL, FI open

requirements.text: The envelope shall treat a heartbeat whose control-loop counter has not advanced for > 0.3 s as missing (SWSR-407).
requirements.acceptance: Frozen counter with live heartbeat → revocation ≤ 0.3 s
requirements.baseline_impl: Not impl: heartbeat carries only `engaged` (`main_comms.h:277-285`)

requirements.text: `pandad` shall send in each heartbeat the frame counter of the latest `carControl` received by `card`/`pandad`.
requirements.acceptance: Counter equals `carControl` frame

requirements.text: The SPI driver shall verify a CRC (polynomial per WP-S-05 §4, OI-7 of WP-S-02) over header and data of every transfer and NACK and discard transfers with a CRC error.
requirements.acceptance: All injected 1–3 bit errors and burst errors ≤ CRC width detected

requirements.text: Each CAN-TX transfer (endpoint 3) shall carry a sequence counter; the envelope shall discard a transfer with a repeated or out-of-order counter and count it as an SPI error.
requirements.acceptance: Replayed, dropped and reordered transfers detected
requirements.baseline_impl: Not impl (`can_comms.h:8-37`)

requirements.acceptance: Interface test VS-SWI

requirements.text: The envelope shall reject actuation frames whose transfer counter is more than 2 control periods older than the newest accepted transfer.
requirements.acceptance: Stale transfer rejected
requirements.baseline_impl: Not impl

requirements.text: The SPI driver shall reject (NACK) a header whose MOSI length exceeds `SPI_BUF_SIZE − SPI_HEADER_SIZE − 1` or whose MISO length exceeds `SPI_BUF_SIZE − 4`, before starting any DMA.
requirements.acceptance: Length = bound accepted; bound + 1 NACKed, no write outside `spi_buf_rx`

requirements.baseline_impl: Not met: `bus_config[param1]` (`main_comms.h:262-264`) (GAP-47); others checked (`:117, 135, 235, 298, 309`)

requirements.acceptance: Fuzzed transfers never write outside `can_write_buffer.data`
requirements.baseline_impl: Partial: bounded by DLC table (`can_comms.h:113-125`); no resync rule; WP-A-02 FFI-SP-03

requirements.text: When SPI errors exceed N_spi within 100 ms while authority is granted, the envelope shall clear authority and report.
requirements.acceptance: Clear on N_spi + 1 errors
requirements.baseline_impl: Partial: counted only (`drivers/spi.h:220-222`, `main_comms.h:36`)

requirements.text: `pandad` shall not forward `sendcan` messages older than 20 ms.
requirements.acceptance: 21 ms message dropped
requirements.baseline_impl: Not met: 1 s (`selfdrive/pandad/pandad.cc:78-79`) (SWSR-614 withdrawn as its duplicate)

requirements.text: The firmware shall service the independent watchdog only at the end of a periodic safety task cycle in which all periodic checks completed (logical checkpoint), never from a comms ISR.
requirements.acceptance: Stall of task, comms ISR storm or main-loop hang → reset ≤ 0.1 s

requirements.text: Every detected fault in the fault table of WP-W-05 §6.1 shall lead to SS-S (SILENT, relay released, CAN TX disabled) within 0.1 s, latched until power cycle or recovered per its documented class.
requirements.acceptance: Each fault injected → SS-S ≤ 0.1 s

requirements.acceptance: ISR storm → SS-S

requirements.text: The TX hook shall count the frames of each whitelisted ID over a sliding 250 ms window (two 125 ms half-windows) and reject a frame when the count reaches the ID's budget (nominal rate with a 1.2× tolerance, plus a burst allowance); while authority is granted, 3 rejected frames within one half-window shall revoke authority and be reported; after such a revocation, authority shall not be granted again until one full 250 ms window has passed without a rejected frame.
requirements.acceptance: `0x2E4` at 2× rate: excess frames rejected; revocation ≤ 0.1 s after the first rejected frame (≤ 0.2 s from flood onset at 2×), as TSR-518 v0.13
requirements.applies_to: CFG-001, reference build only (`LIONDRIVER_REFERENCE=1`); other builds keep the upstream behaviour
requirements.baseline_impl: Impl (reference build, opendbc `7993399`, panda `8aa8671`): `tx_rate_check` (`opendbc/safety/safety.h`), Toyota budgets (`modes/toyota.h`), health flag bit 11 → `pandaState.txRateExceeded`; unit tests `test_tx_rate_*` (flood, sliding window, host cadence, revocation timing, catch-up bursts, no limit-state update); HIL `tests/hitl/test_14_tx_rate.py` (not run). Design DN-01 (assurance/05-software/design-notes/DN-01-tx-rate-supervision.md). Re-engagement block (amendment, ATC-20): not at the pinned opendbc; proposed change change-2026-10-13-tx-rate-reengagement (assurance/07-supporting/impact/change-2026-10-13-tx-rate-reengagement.md)
