requirements.text: The firmware shall activate its siren within 0.5 s, without SoC involvement, when (a) the heartbeat is lost (SWSR-407) while authority was granted within the last 5 s; (b) authority is cleared while granted for any reason other than a brake press (SWSR-302) or PCM cruise inactive (SWSR-301): RX fault (SWSR-406), EPS fault (SWSR-110), rejected command (SWSR-108), TX failure or bus-off (SWSR-508), platform fault (SWSR-502) or heartbeat "not engaged" (SWSR-307); (c) SWSR-516b fires.
requirements.acceptance: Siren ≤ 0.5 s for each trigger; no siren on a brake press or PCM cancel alone
requirements.baseline_impl: Partial: heartbeat loss (SWSR-407) revoking authority that was granted → 3 s siren at once, ≈ 0.56 s after the last heartbeat (0.3 s + 10 ms + 2 × 125 ms speaker tick), all builds (panda `c33343b`, `drivers/heartbeat_siren.h`, host test `tests/heartbeat_siren`, HIL `tests/hitl/test_15_heartbeat_siren.py` not run); 1 Hz path unchanged: 3 s siren after 4–5 s heartbeat loss (`main.c:169-171, 198-201`), the only siren when authority ended within the 5 s before the loss; EPS fault (SWSR-110) persisting 1 s while authority is granted → siren ≥ 3 s (panda `b790fca`, `drivers/eps_fault_siren.h`, host test `tests/eps_fault_siren`; HIL not run). Other (b) triggers and (c) not impl

requirements.text: τ_max(v) shall be a speed-dependent lookup derived on the reference vehicle by (1) characterising the steady-state lateral acceleration and wheel torque produced by raw requests 0…1500 at speeds 10…120 km/h (AOU-01R), (2) choosing per speed the largest request whose worst-case lateral deviation over the driver intervention time stays inside the bound of WP-S-04 §3 (assurance/03-system/WP-S-04-timing-ftti-budget.md), and (3) confirming controllability C1 for that bound with the tests of WP-C-08 (assurance/02-concept/WP-C-08-driver-hmi-misuse-analysis.md) §8. The speed value used shall be the one that yields the smaller torque bound when the speed estimate is uncertain.

The mechanism exists (`lateral.h:66-71`) but uses `vehicle_speed.min − 1 m/s`, which is conservative only if τ_max increases with speed; the direction must be checked against the derived table (OI-3). Speed input integrity: TSR-405(a). GAP-04

requirements.text: If the envelope rejects a lateral command frame while lateral authority is granted, it shall revoke lateral authority (SS-L) and keep it revoked until a new valid engagement (TSR-301), and it shall report the event and its cause to the SoC.
requirements.timing: detect: same frame / react: same frame
requirements.baseline_impl: Not implemented: the violating frame is dropped and the rate state reset (`lateral.h:140-148`), `safety_tx_blocked` is counted and reported (`drivers/can_common.h:168-171`, `main_comms.h:27`), but `controls_allowed` is not cleared. Upstream design lets the host recover; the FSC requires latching (OI-4)

requirements.text: Whenever the envelope rejects a `0x2E4` frame or revokes lateral authority, the EPS shall receive torque 0 with STEER_REQUEST 0 within ≤ 0.1 s. This shall be achieved by (a) the envelope transmitting, in place of each rejected frame, a `0x2E4` frame with zero torque, STEER_REQUEST 0, a counter continuing the host sequence and a valid checksum; or (b) only if vehicle characterisation shows that the EPS ramps LKA torque to zero within ≤ 0.1 s of a missing `0x2E4` frame, by withholding the frame. Option (a) is the recommended design.
requirements.baseline_impl: **Not implemented / unverified.** Rejecting a frame drops it (`drivers/can_common.h:161-176`); the EPS then sees a message drop-out. The only available description of drop-out handling is a code comment (LKA_STATE 9 → 11 over ≈2 s, then 3; `carstate.py:15-16`), so torque may persist after rejection. NF-02, GAP-05

requirements.text: The envelope shall receive EPS_STATUS (`0x262`) and, while lateral authority is granted, shall revoke lateral authority and report the cause when LKA_STATE indicates an EPS fault or LKA unavailability, or when EPS_STATUS is missing beyond its timeout (TSR-401). The LKA_STATE fault code set shall be confirmed for the reference EPS firmware.
requirements.asil: B (SG-02); B‡ where it gates SG-01
requirements.baseline_impl: **Partial** (reference build; not yet verified on the vehicle): `0x262` is an envelope RX check (checksum, 5-period timeout at a nominal 25 Hz, gates engagement via TSR-306; opendbc `98404a4`), and while LKA_STATE is in the host's fault set {0, 3, 9, 11, 17, 21, 25} STEERING_LKA frames with torque or a steer request are refused (opendbc `242d63d`, IA EPS fault (assurance/07-supporting/impact/change-2026-10-12-opendbc-toyota-eps-fault.md)). The cause is reported to the host: health flag `HEALTH_FLAG_EPS_FAULT` → `pandaState.epsFault`, logged by `pandad` on each change (panda `877730e`, opendbc `adcb7c2`). **Open:** confirmation of the fault code set for the reference EPS firmware. GAP-03

requirements.text: The EPS shall limit the LKA torque at the steering wheel to ≤ T_EPS for any `0x2E4` request and remove LKA torque within t_EPS after `0x2E4` stops or STEER_REQUEST clears. (External measure; T_EPS and t_EPS to be measured.)
requirements.baseline_impl: Unverified (AOU-01R, GAP-05)

requirements.text: The envelope shall reject every ACC_CONTROL (`0x343`) frame whose ACCEL_CMD exceeds a_max, where a_max is derived from the controllability of HE-03.1…03.3 on the reference vehicle. Baseline a_max = +2.0 m/s² (raw 2000).
requirements.baseline_impl: Implemented without rationale: `modes/toyota.h:207-210, 225`; `longitudinal.h:8-12`. Host uses 2.0 m/s² under `RAISED_ACCEL_LIMIT` (`values.py:39-43`, `interface.py:117-118`), zero margin; flag not validated for the Corolla (GAP-04)

requirements.text: The envelope shall reject every `0x343` frame whose ACCEL_CMD is below a_min, derived from the controllability of HE-04.1 (following traffic). Baseline a_min = −3.5 m/s² (raw −3500).
requirements.baseline_impl: Implemented without rationale: `modes/toyota.h:209` (GAP-04)

requirements.text: While longitudinal authority is not granted (not engaged, or accelerator pressed per TSR-305), the envelope shall accept `0x343` only with the inactive acceleration value.
requirements.baseline_impl: Implemented: `longitudinal.h:3-12`

requirements.text: The envelope shall reject `0x343` frames whose ACCEL_CMD increases, relative to the last accepted value (the inactive value counting as 0 m/s² at engagement), faster than j_up, derived from controllability.
requirements.baseline_impl: Not implemented in the envelope (GAP-04). Host-only wind-up limit 0.12 m/s² per 3-frame step ≈ 4 m/s³ (`carcontroller.py:21`)

requirements.text: The envelope shall reject `0x343` frames whose ACCEL_CMD decreases (deceleration onset) faster than j_down, derived from following-traffic controllability.
requirements.baseline_impl: Not implemented in the envelope (GAP-04). Host-only wind-down ≈ −4 m/s³ (`carcontroller.py:22`)

requirements.text: On revocation of longitudinal authority the transition to SS-G shall not cause a vehicle deceleration or acceleration step beyond the jerk bounds of TSR-204/205. If the PCM response to a step from the last commanded value to the inactive value is not shown to be bounded (AOU-05R), the envelope shall accept a commanded value that winds down to the inactive value at no more than j_down/j_up for at most 1 s after revocation.
requirements.baseline_impl: Not specified. Today any non-inactive value is rejected at once after revocation (`longitudinal.h:8-12`); vehicle response unknown (GAP-05)

requirements.text: For `0x343`, the envelope shall also check the actuation-relevant fields PERMIT_BRAKING, CANCEL_REQ, RELEASE_STANDSTILL and ACCEL_CMD_ALT against the values allowed in the current authority state, and while authority is not granted shall accept only frames that do not request acceleration, braking or standstill release.
requirements.baseline_impl: Partial: in openpilot-longitudinal mode only bytes 0–1 (ACCEL_CMD) are checked (`modes/toyota.h:216-241`); field layout `opendbc_repo/opendbc/dbc/generator/toyota/_toyota_2017.dbc:178-193`. NF-03

requirements.text: The PCM shall bound ACC acceleration requests to its own ACC envelope, honour CANCEL_REQ, and produce coasting without a deceleration step on the inactive value. (External measure.)
requirements.baseline_impl: Unverified (AOU-05R, GAP-05)

requirements.text: The envelope shall grant actuation authority only on the rising edge of PCM_CRUISE (`0x1D2`) CRUISE_ACTIVE, and only once the SoC heartbeat reports the item engaged within 1 s of that edge (otherwise not until the next rising edge), and shall revoke it in the same frame in which CRUISE_ACTIVE is received false (cancel, main switch off, PCM-internal drop).
requirements.timing: detect ≤ 1 period (30 ms at 33 Hz) / same frame
requirements.baseline_impl: Implemented: `safety.h:518-527`; `modes/toyota.h:143-146`. `0x1D2` has a checksum but no counter (GAP-01) → TSR-402…405. 2026-10-14, reference build: the heartbeat condition (WP-A-05 LS-06): the edge opens a 1 s window, the grant is made in the safety task once `heartbeat_engaged` is set; cancelled by cruise off, brake, an RX fault or a mode change (opendbc `9a13f60`, jherrodthomas/opendbc#14 (https://github.com/jherrodthomas/opendbc/pull/14)); unit-tested, not verified on the vehicle

requirements.text: The envelope shall revoke all actuation authority when a driver brake press is received (rising edge, or pressed while the vehicle is moving).
requirements.timing: detect ≤ 1 period (25 ms at 40 Hz) / same frame; SS-L via TSR-109
requirements.baseline_impl: Implemented: `safety.h:350-356`; BRAKE_MODULE (`0x226`) bit 37 `modes/toyota.h:148-150`; `vehicle_moving` from wheel speeds `modes/toyota.h:157-168`. `0x226` has no checksum and no counter (`modes/toyota.h:46`, GAP-01) → TSR-405(b)

requirements.text: On every fault-induced disengagement, with or without openpilot longitudinal, the SoC shall set CANCEL_REQ so that the PCM drops ACC. The PCM cruise state then changes, which changes the cluster cruise indication (TSR-309, AOU-12) and makes the envelope revoke (TSR-301); a cancel without effect is caught by TSR-516(c).
requirements.baseline_impl: Implemented on host: cancel whenever PCM cruise is on and the item is not enabled (`openpilot/selfdrive/controls/controlsd.py:162`), sent in ACC_CONTROL in both longitudinal modes (`opendbc_repo/opendbc/car/toyota/carcontroller.py:253-254, 269-273`). The host replaces the PCM's own fault sound on a forced cancel with its own UI sound (`carcontroller.py:283-287`); whether the PCM sound is an independent cue is part of AOU-12

requirements.text: The envelope shall monitor STEER_TORQUE_DRIVER (`0x260`) on the LKA path and (a) reject `0x2E4` frames that increase torque opposing the driver beyond a driver allowance (driver-limited check in addition to the measured-torque check of TSR-104), and (b) when the driver torque exceeds T_ovr for longer than t_ovr, revoke lateral authority or force the commanded torque to zero at the Δ_down rate. T_ovr, t_ovr and the allowance shall be derived from the override behaviour accepted in WP-C-08 (assurance/02-concept/WP-C-08-driver-hmi-misuse-analysis.md) and from the EPS override threshold (AOU-02R).
requirements.timing: detect ≤ 2 frames of `0x260` (40 ms) / torque decreasing next frame, zero ≤ 0.2 s
requirements.baseline_impl: **Not implemented on the LKA path** (GAP-02). Driver torque is sampled (`modes/toyota.h:113-116`) but used only for LTA (`modes/toyota.h:294-298`). A driver-limited check exists (`lateral.h:26-46`, `TorqueDriverLimited`) but the Toyota mode is motor-limited (`modes/toyota.h:178`). Host-only: `MAX_USER_TORQUE` 500 (`carcontroller.py:33, 83`)

requirements.text: While the accelerator is pressed (PCM_CRUISE GAS_RELEASED = 0), the envelope shall withdraw longitudinal authority (inactive value only, TSR-203). The accelerator shall not revoke lateral authority in the reference configuration unless the HMI decision in WP-C-08 changes `DisengageOnAccelerator`.
requirements.baseline_impl: Implemented: `modes/toyota.h:146`; `longitudinal.h:3-5`. `DisengageOnAccelerator` default `0` (`common/params_keys.h:35`)

requirements.text: The envelope shall not grant actuation authority while any RX check of TSR-401…405 is failed, including timeouts not yet evaluated by the periodic check.
requirements.baseline_impl: **Met for the existing checks** (opendbc `aff4033`): for Toyota, a PCM rising edge grants authority only if every RX check is seen, valid and not lagging at that moment (`rx_checks_allow_engagement()` in `safety.h`). Frozen-value and cross-checks do not exist yet (IA RX timeout (assurance/07-supporting/impact/change-2026-10-12-opendbc-toyota-rx-timeout.md) §7)

requirements.text: (a) The envelope shall revoke authority when the SoC heartbeat reports "not engaged" while authority is granted, within ≤ 0.3 s. (b) The SoC shall immediately disable when the envelope's reported authority differs from its own engaged state for > 0.3 s.
requirements.baseline_impl: (a) 3 consecutive 1 Hz ticks ≈ 2–3 s (`main.c:181-189`). (b) 200 cycles at 100 Hz = 2 s (`selfdrive/selfdrived/selfdrived.py:338, 503-510`) (GAP-06)

requirements.text: If PCM cruise is active while the item is not engaged, or the item is engaged while PCM cruise is inactive, for longer than 1 s, the SoC shall warn the driver and request ACC cancel.
requirements.baseline_impl: Implemented, not verified on the vehicle: `cruiseMismatch` after 1 s with a repeating prompt (`selfdrive/selfdrived/selfdrived.py`, `events.py`); `controlsd` keeps requesting the cancel. The other direction (engaged while PCM cruise is off) disengages through `pcmDisable` on PCM-cruise cars (GAP-19 closed in code)

requirements.text: The engagement state enforced by the envelope shall be the PCM cruise state, so that the vehicle's cluster cruise indicator is an indication of engagement independent of the item's HMI.
requirements.baseline_impl: Implemented by TSR-301 design. Independence of the cluster indication unverified (AOU-12)

requirements.text: Driver brake application shall produce braking regardless of `0x343` content, and the PCM shall drop ACC on brake. (External measure.)
requirements.baseline_impl: Unverified (AOU-03R)

requirements.text: Actuation authority shall be false at MCU start-up and after every safety-mode change, and all limiter state (last torque, rate windows, samples) shall be reset.
requirements.baseline_impl: Implemented: `safety.h:57, 423-460`

requirements.text: For each RX message used for gating or limiting (`0xAA`, `0x260`, `0x1D2`, `0x226`, and `0x262`, `0x1D3`, `0xB4` once added), the envelope shall detect absence longer than 5 nominal periods and shall evaluate this at ≥ 50 Hz, so that worst-case detection is ≤ 0.2 s.
requirements.baseline_impl: **Met for the four Toyota RX checks, not yet verified on hardware** (opendbc `aff4033`, panda `9f60e17`): lag after 5 nominal periods (`safety_config.rx_timeout_periods`, `modes/toyota.h`), evaluated at 100 Hz in the panda safety task, so detection ≤ 0.16 s. In the reference build `0x262` (25 Hz) and `0x1D3` (33 Hz) are also RX checks (opendbc `98404a4`; nominal rates from openpilot's former CAN parser minimums, to be measured, WP-S-05 OI-7). `0xB4` is not in the RX set: no nominal rate known (IA RX timeout (assurance/07-supporting/impact/change-2026-10-12-opendbc-toyota-rx-timeout.md) §8)

requirements.text: The envelope shall verify the Toyota checksum and the message length of every RX message that carries a checksum (`0x260`, `0x1D2`, and `0x262`, `0x1D3`, `0xB4` once added) and treat one failed frame as an RX fault.
requirements.baseline_impl: Implemented for `0x260`, `0x1D2`: `safety.h:164-197`; `modes/toyota.h:40-46, 65-77`. Residual weakness: 8-bit additive sum (GAP-01)

requirements.text: The envelope shall detect when an RX message arrives at more than 1.5× its nominal rate over a 100 ms window (indicating duplicated or inserted frames) and treat it as an RX fault.
requirements.baseline_impl: Not implemented (GAP-01). `frequency` is only used for the timeout (`safety.h:330-336`)

requirements.text: For RX signals that vary in normal operation, the envelope shall detect a frozen payload: an identical data field (excluding checksum) for longer than t_frz while the vehicle is moving (`0x260` torque/angle bytes; `0xAA` wheel speeds above a minimum speed; `0xB4` ENCODER). t_frz shall be set from fork-owned drive logs so that no false detection occurs in the reference log set.
requirements.baseline_impl: Not implemented (GAP-01)

requirements.text: The envelope shall apply these cross-checks and treat a disagreement lasting longer than its tolerance time as an RX fault: (a) wheel-speed mean (`0xAA`) vs SPEED (`0xB4`) within 2 m/s; (b) BRAKE_PRESSED in `0x226` vs PCM_CRUISE_2 (`0x1D3`) BRAKE_PRESSED — on disagreement the envelope shall assume "brake pressed" (revoke); (c) CRUISE_ACTIVE = 1 shall imply PCM_CRUISE_2 MAIN_ON = 1; (d) while authority is granted, measured EPS torque shall follow the accepted command within an EPS-response tolerance (detects frozen or replaced `0x260`). Signal availability and tolerances shall be confirmed on reference-vehicle logs.
requirements.baseline_impl: **Partial** (reference build, opendbc `875e325`, IA cruise/main (assurance/07-supporting/impact/change-2026-10-12-opendbc-toyota-cruise-main.md)): (c) CRUISE_ACTIVE with `0x1D3` MAIN_ON = 0 refuses engagement at once and revokes authority after a 150 ms disagreement. **Not implemented:** (a) speed cross-check (`0xB4` not in the RX set, no nominal rate); (b) BRAKE_PRESSED cross-check, pending the meaning of the `0x1D3` bit (driver pedal or any braking, ACC included) from reference logs; (d) EPS-response check (GAP-01). A speed cross-check helper exists but is unused by the Toyota mode (`safety.h:529-537`). Candidate signals: `0xB4` SPEED/ENCODER (`opendbc_repo/opendbc/dbc/generator/toyota/_toyota_2017.dbc:77-80`), `0x1D3` BRAKE_PRESSED (`_toyota_2017.dbc:110-111`)

requirements.text: On any RX fault of TSR-401…405, the envelope shall revoke all actuation authority within ≤ 0.1 s (SS-L via TSR-109, SS-G), report a fault-specific reason code to the SoC, and not grant authority again until all checks pass and a new PCM rising edge occurs.
requirements.baseline_impl: Partial: revocation on checksum/quality (`safety.h:112-121`) and timeout (`safety.h:337-340`); only a single flag is reported (`main_comms.h:23`)

requirements.text: In a car safety mode, the envelope shall detect absence of the SoC heartbeat (`0xf3`) for > 0.3 s and then revoke all actuation authority at once (SS-L, SS-G). It shall enter SS-S (SILENT, relay released) after the longer timeout of TSR-510.
requirements.baseline_impl: **Partial, not yet verified on hardware** (panda `c2e5d93`): in a car mode the 100 Hz safety task revokes all authority once no heartbeat has arrived for 0.3 s (`drivers/heartbeat_monitor.h`); the host sends it at 10 Hz. SILENT still follows after 5 s (TSR-510). Open: safety-task latency under load (WP-W-03 §5.4), HIL (IA heartbeat (assurance/07-supporting/impact/change-2026-10-12-panda-fast-heartbeat.md))

requirements.text: While lateral authority is granted, the envelope shall monitor the arrival of `0x2E4` frames from the SoC and, if no frame arrives for > 50 ms (5 frames), revoke authority and command SS-L (TSR-109). While longitudinal authority is granted, the same shall apply to `0x343` with a gap > 100 ms.
requirements.baseline_impl: **Implemented in the reference build, not yet verified on hardware** (opendbc `273f44e`, opendbc#11): while authority is granted, the 100 Hz safety task revokes it when `0x2E4` has not reached the TX hook for > 50 ms or, with openpilot longitudinal, `0x343` for > 100 ms (`safety.h` `tx_arrival_ok`, `modes/toyota.h`). SS-L follows from the revocation (TSR-109). Open: thresholds on reference logs, HIL (IA TX arrival (assurance/07-supporting/impact/change-2026-10-12-opendbc-toyota-tx-arrival.md))

requirements.text: The heartbeat shall carry evidence that the control loop is alive (e.g. the latest `carControl` frame counter), and the envelope shall treat a heartbeat whose evidence has not advanced for > 0.3 s as a missing heartbeat.
requirements.baseline_impl: Not implemented: heartbeat carries only `engaged` = `selfdriveState` alive && valid && enabled (`selfdrive/pandad/pandad.cc:389-390`) (GAP-10)

requirements.text: Every SPI transfer (header and data) shall be protected by a CRC whose residual error probability over the maximum transfer length meets the target set in WP-S-05 §4 (assurance/03-system/WP-S-05-hsi-specification.md), and every CAN-TX transfer shall carry a sequence counter; the envelope shall discard transfers with a failed CRC or a repeated or out-of-order counter. The per-packet XOR may remain as an additional check.
requirements.baseline_impl: Not met: 8-bit XOR seeded 0xAB on header and data (`drivers/spi.h:97-104, 122, 137`); per-CAN-packet 8-bit XOR (`drivers/can_common.h:144-159`, checked at FDCAN TX `drivers/fdcan.h:100`); no sequence counter (`can_comms.h:8-37`) (GAP-10)

requirements.text: The envelope shall reject actuation frames whose transfer counter shows they are older than 2 control periods relative to the newest accepted transfer (freshness).
requirements.baseline_impl: Not implemented (GAP-10). Host-side age check is 1 s (`selfdrive/pandad/pandad.cc:78-79`), see TSR-614

requirements.text: The envelope shall validate every length field received over SPI against its buffer size before starting a DMA transfer or copy, and every control-request parameter used as an array index against the array bounds; a violation shall be NACKed and counted as an SPI error.
requirements.baseline_impl: **Not met (NF-04):** MOSI/MISO lengths are taken from the header (`drivers/spi.h:115-116`) and the data DMA is started with `spi_data_len_mosi + 1` into a 4096-byte buffer (`drivers/spi.h:233`, `drivers/drivers.h:216`) without a bound check; `comms_can_read` fills `spi_buf_tx` up to the requested MISO length (`drivers/spi.h:150`); request `0xe8` indexes `bus_config[param1]` without a bound check (`main_comms.h:262-264`). The nominal host keeps lengths below the buffer size (`selfdrive/pandad/spi.cc:319-320`), but freedom from interference cannot rely on the QM host

requirements.text: If SPI errors (header/data checksum failures, NACKs) exceed a rate threshold while authority is granted, the envelope shall revoke authority and report.
requirements.baseline_impl: Partial: counted and reported only (`drivers/spi.h:220-222`, `main_comms.h:36`)

requirements.text: The safety MCU shall be supervised by an independent hardware watchdog (IWDG1, LSI-clocked) that is started no later than the first time the harness relay is energised after a reset, by any path (safety-mode change or configuration/debug command), and then stays active until the next reset; that cannot be stopped by the SoC; that is serviced only after the periodic safety processing has completed; and that resets the MCU within ≤ 0.1 s of a stall (SG-07 FDTI, WP-S-04 (assurance/03-system/WP-S-04-timing-ftti-budget.md) §3.6; ≤ 0.2 s would meet SG-01 only). Rationale for the start condition (amended in v0.4): until the relay is first energised after a reset, the stock camera-to-vehicle path is intact and no actuation frame reaches the vehicle, so a stall cannot violate SG-01 or SG-07; an idle device keeps its power-save and stop modes.
requirements.baseline_impl: **Implemented, not yet verified on hardware** (panda `3859fa8`): IWDG1 started the first time the relay is energised, on any path (`drivers/harness.h`); fed from the 100 Hz safety task only after main-loop progress (`drivers/hw_watchdog.h`, `main.c`); 90 ms nominal; window mode, about 5 ms minimum feed interval (HWSR-501b). a watchdog reset is reported to the host (`pandaState.watchdogReset`). Open: LSI range at both ends, HIL evidence (IA watchdog (assurance/07-supporting/impact/change-2026-10-12-panda-hw-watchdog.md))

requirements.text: Every detected MCU fault (watchdog, interrupt-rate, register divergence, memory ECC, clock, supply, temperature, SPI/DMA, siren, relay) shall lead to SS-S within ≤ 0.1 s of detection. Faults shall be classified as latching until power cycle or as recoverable, by documented rationale. During and after any reset the outputs shall be in SS-S until a valid safety mode is set.
requirements.baseline_impl: **Not implemented.** Faults are report-only (`sys/faults.h:8-27`); `PERMANENT_FAULTS 0U` (`sys/sys.h:50`); only relay malfunction blocks TX (GAP-08). Start state SILENT (`main.c:295`). A hang (default handlers, `assert_fatal`, no IWDG) leaves the relay in its last state (GAP-43). HWSR-502…502c

requirements.text: Memory faults that can corrupt actuation decisions shall be detected: RAM ECC with double-error reaction, flash image CRC at start-up and periodically, and periodic check of safety-critical configuration registers, each leading to TSR-502.
requirements.timing: ≤ 0.2 s for RAM/register faults; flash: start-up + background
requirements.baseline_impl: Partial: register divergence check at 1 Hz, report-only (`drivers/registers.h:56-70`, `main.c:228-229`); no ECC handling, no runtime CRC (GAP-08). HWSR-503…503d

requirements.text: Loss or drift of the MCU clock that would invalidate timing checks or CAN bit timing shall be detected and lead to TSR-502.
requirements.baseline_impl: Partial: HSE clock security system per WP-H-01 HWSR-504; no frequency cross-check

requirements.text: Supply voltage of the MCU outside its operating range shall lead to reset or SS-S (brown-out reset, programmable voltage detector), and vehicle input voltage out of range while the relay is driven shall lead to SS-S.
requirements.baseline_impl: Unknown / not implemented (BOR, PVD not configured; input voltage reported only, `main_comms.h:14`). HWSR-505…505b

requirements.text: The intercept relay shall be de-energise-to-safe, its actual state shall be read back and compared with the commanded state in both directions within ≤ 0.3 s, and a detected relay malfunction shall inhibit all actuation TX and be latched until power cycle (not cleared by a safety-mode change).
requirements.baseline_impl: Partial: open-drain active-low drive, released at init (`drivers/harness.h:8-33, 96-107`); indirect detection only (camera control messages on the car side) after a 1 s transition window counted at 1 Hz (`safety.h:211-220, 372-380`); cleared on every mode change (`safety.h:427, 459`), so a host can clear it with `0xdc`. No readback (GAP-12); relay stuck in intercept not detected at all (GAP-43). HWSR-506…506d

requirements.text: Safety-critical data (safety mode and parameter, limits, authority state, relay state) and the stacks shall be protected against writes from communication handlers by the MPU, with a stack guard, and a MemManage fault shall lead to TSR-502.
requirements.baseline_impl: Not implemented: no MPU configuration (GAP-08, GAP-11). HWSR-507

requirements.text: The car-side CAN transceiver shall be non-transmitting from reset until enabled by firmware; bus-off or persistent TX failure on the car-side bus while authority is granted shall revoke authority and be reported.
requirements.baseline_impl: Partial: transceivers enabled after SILENT (`main.c:295-298`); bus-off counted (`drivers/fdcan.h`), host raises `canError` only. HWSR-508…508c

requirements.text: MCU die temperature outside its specified range shall lead to SS-S.
requirements.baseline_impl: Partial: DTS read and reported only (`main_comms.h:51-52`). HWSR-509

requirements.text: Ignition state shall be sensed from the harness ignition line; loss of the SoC heartbeat shall lead to SS-S after ≤ 2 s regardless of the ignition reading, and a failed ignition input shall not keep the relay driven without a heartbeat.
requirements.baseline_impl: Partial: line-only ignition for Toyota (`drivers/harness.h:35-52`; `opendbc_repo/opendbc/safety/ignition.h:12-63` has no Toyota case); SILENT after 5 s (ignition on) / 2 s (off) (`main.c:101-103, 193`). HWSR-510…510a

requirements.text: Only release-signed LionDriver firmware shall execute on the safety MCU: the signature scheme shall use a current algorithm and key length, flash read-out and write protection shall be set, the SoC's control of `STM_BOOT0`/`STM_RST_N` shall not allow non-release code to drive the relay, release builds of `pandad` shall not flash a development bootstub, and softloader entry (`0xd1` param 1) shall be refused in a car safety mode and while the ignition is on (CSR-024).
requirements.baseline_impl: **Not met.** RSA-1024/SHA-1 (`crypto/rsa.h:37`, `crypto/sha.h:45`; `bootstub.c:47-72`); only sector 0 protected from erase (`stm32h7/llflash.h:12-20`); SoC drives BOOT0/NRST (`openpilot/common/hardware/comma/hardware.py:400-419`); recovery flashes a development bootstub (`selfdrive/pandad/pandad.py:34-39`); softloader entry allowed in release at any time (`main_comms.h:176-180`) (GAP-24, GAP-38). See WP-S-07 (assurance/03-system/WP-S-07-cybersecurity-requirements-architecture.md)

requirements.text: In release builds for the reference configuration the safety MCU shall accept only the modes SILENT, NOOUTPUT, ELM327 (fingerprinting, relay released) and TOYOTA with the reference safety parameter compiled into the firmware (EPS factor 73, no flags). Once TOYOTA mode is active, it shall accept only a change to NOOUTPUT or SILENT; any other request shall be rejected and reported. The alternative-experience word shall likewise be fixed to the reference value in release builds, so that it cannot be changed in a non-car mode and carried into a later TOYOTA session.
requirements.baseline_impl: **Met in the reference build, not yet verified on hardware** (`LIONDRIVER_REFERENCE=1`, panda `3859fa8`): `0xdc` accepts only SILENT, NOOUTPUT, ELM327 and TOYOTA with parameter 73; in TOYOTA only NOOUTPUT or SILENT; `0xdf` refused, alternative experience stays 0 (`board/reference_lock.h`). Refused requests are counted in the health packet and published as `pandaState.requestsRejected`, and `pandad` logs them; no driver-facing alert yet. AOU-14 (IA mode lock (assurance/07-supporting/impact/change-2026-10-12-panda-safety-mode-lock.md))

requirements.text: In release builds, control requests that can change actuation, relay, CAN configuration or comms state shall be rejected while a car safety mode is active: at least `0xc5` (relay drive), `0xe5` (CAN loopback), `0xde`/`0xf9`/`0xfc`/`0xe8` (bit rate and CAN-FD configuration), `0xdb` (OBD multiplexing), `0xe6` (clock source), `0xe7` (power save; in car mode it stops camera-side forwarding with the relay energised, SG-07, WP-A-04 SPF-08), `0xf1` (queue clear), `0xd1` param 1 (softloader entry, see also TSR-511), `0xd8` (MCU reset without fault reporting), `0xdf` (alternative experience, see TSR-512). Also `0xc0` (comms reset), `0xb0`/`0xb1` and `0xf6` (to be confirmed per WP-W-02 OI-5).
requirements.baseline_impl: **Partial, reference build only** (panda `9f60e17`): `0xc5`, `0xd8`, `0xdb`, `0xde`, `0xe5`, `0xe6`, `0xe7`, `0xe8`, `0xf1`, `0xf9`, `0xfc` and `0xd1` param 1 refused in a car mode (`board/reference_lock.h`). `0xc0`, `0xb0`, `0xb1`, `0xf6` still to be confirmed (WP-W-02 OI-5) (IA mode lock (assurance/07-supporting/impact/change-2026-10-12-panda-safety-mode-lock.md))

requirements.text: Release firmware shall be built without `ALLOW_DEBUG`, with the LionDriver release key, and shall not contain the ALLOUTPUT mode, debug-only safety modes or debug-key acceptance; the build type shall be readable through the version request and recorded in the release record.
requirements.baseline_impl: Not met by default: DEBUG + `ALLOW_DEBUG` unless `RELEASE` and `CERT` are set (`panda/SConscript:12-20`); debug modes `safety.h:413-422`; debug key `bootstub.c:66-71` (GAP-25). The reference build is reported in the health packet (`HEALTH_FLAG_REFERENCE_BUILD`, panda `6dee6fa`) and `pandad` configures a car safety mode only on a panda that reports it (`selfdrive/pandad/panda_safety.cc`, SWSR-514h); the debug/release build type is not yet reported

requirements.text: At every power-up, before the relay is first driven, the safety MCU shall run start-up tests of its safety mechanisms (flash CRC, RAM test of safety data regions, watchdog reset path at a defined interval, relay drive and readback, siren path) and stay in SS-S and report if any test fails.
requirements.baseline_impl: Not implemented (latent-fault handling absent)

requirements.text: The safety MCU shall sound its own acoustic warning within ≤ 0.5 s of detection, without depending on SoC software, when (a) the SoC heartbeat is lost (TSR-407) while authority was granted within the last 5 s; (b) the envelope revokes authority while it is granted for any reason other than a driver action that the envelope itself observes (brake press, TSR-302; PCM cruise inactive, TSR-301), that is on an RX fault (TSR-406), an EPS fault state (TSR-110), a rejected command (TSR-108), a car-side TX failure or bus-off (TSR-508), a platform fault (TSR-502) or a heartbeat "not engaged" (TSR-307(a)); or (c) PCM cruise is still active more than 0.5 s after the SoC heartbeat first reported "not engaged" (a fault-induced disengagement whose ACC cancel, TSR-303, had no effect).
requirements.baseline_impl: Partial: (a) heartbeat loss: siren for 3 s at once when the 0.3 s heartbeat monitor (TSR-407) revokes authority that was granted, ≤ 0.3 s + 10 ms + 250 ms ≈ 0.56 s after the last heartbeat, in all builds (panda `c33343b`, `drivers/heartbeat_siren.h`, IA fast heartbeat (assurance/07-supporting/impact/change-2026-10-12-panda-fast-heartbeat.md) §5; not verified on hardware); the 1 Hz path (siren for 3 s after 4–5 s heartbeat loss if authority within the last 5 s, `main.c:169-171, 198-201`) unchanged, and alone covers authority that ended within the 5 s before the loss; (b) for the EPS fault (TSR-110): siren once the fault has persisted 1 s while authority is granted, ≥ 3 s, ≤ 0.26 s after that detection (worst case: the speaker sounds only on every other 8 Hz tick) (panda `b790fca`, `drivers/eps_fault_siren.h`, IA EPS fault (assurance/07-supporting/impact/change-2026-10-12-opendbc-toyota-eps-fault.md) §7; detection defined as 1 s persistence by maintainer decision 2026-10-12, to be confirmed against fault durations in reference logs); other (b) triggers and (c) not implemented; siren path via codec over I2C on some boards, malfunction reported only (`drivers/fake_siren.h:38-52`); shared speaker with SoC audio to be analysed in DFA (WP-A-03 (assurance/08-analyses/WP-A-03-dependent-failure-analysis.md))

requirements.text: Corruption of an approved actuation frame after the TX hook (copy into FDCAN message RAM, message RAM, FDCAN core, transceiver) shall be detected, e.g. by reading back the safety MCU's own transmitted frames on the car-side bus and comparing them with the approved frame, and a mismatch shall lead to TSR-502.
requirements.baseline_impl: **Not implemented.** Packet XOR checked before the FDCAN load only (`drivers/fdcan.h:100`); no read-back after load (WP-A-04 SPF-02, SFMEA-17)

requirements.text: The envelope shall supervise the transmit rate of each actuation message ID (`0x2E4`, `0x343`, `0x412`, and any other TX-whitelisted ID) against its nominal period and reject frames sent faster than the nominal rate plus a defined tolerance; persistent excess while authority is granted shall revoke authority and be reported.
requirements.timing: per frame; revoke ≤ 0.1 s after the first rejected frame (DN-01 (assurance/05-software/design-notes/DN-01-tx-rate-supervision.md) D-6; ≤ 0.2 s from the onset of a flood at 2× the nominal rate)
requirements.baseline_impl: **Met in the reference build, not yet verified on hardware** (opendbc `7993399`, panda `8aa8671`, IA TX rate (assurance/07-supporting/impact/change-2026-10-12-tx-rate-supervision.md)): per-ID count over a sliding 250 ms window with budgets for every TX-whitelisted ID; frames beyond the budget rejected before the content checks; 3 rejections in a half-window while authority is granted revoke it, reported as `pandaState.txRateExceeded`. Budgets to be confirmed on reference logs (DN-01 §9). RX rate is TSR-403

requirements.text: The safety MCU shall have a documented interrupt-priority and execution-timing scheme: priorities assigned explicitly for every enabled interrupt; safety hooks, CAN TX and SoC command dispatch either moved out of interrupt context or bounded by measured WCET; and the worst-case latency of the periodic safety processing (timeouts, heartbeat, watchdog service) shown to meet the TSR-401/407/501 budgets under worst-case interrupt load.
requirements.baseline_impl: **Partial** (panda `52cad44`): every enabled interrupt has an explicit priority, all at one level until the WP-W-03 §5.4.2 scheme is adopted; R-1 and R-8 races closed, R-2 bounded at 10 ms. **Not implemented:** WCET and latency measurement (WP-W-03 §5.4.5); RX hook in the FDCAN interrupt (`drivers/fdcan.h:221, 245-252`); TX hook and control-request dispatch in the SPI DMA interrupt (`stm32h7/llspi.h:56-60`, `drivers/spi.h:143, 162`, `can_comms.h:97, 118`) (GAP-50)

requirements.text: `selfdrived` shall classify faults as (i) untrusted command or input (loss or staleness of an input to the control law, model failure, CAN error, controls mismatch) → immediate disable, and (ii) trustworthy but degrading (thermal, storage, memory) → soft disable. Actuation on an input that has failed its alive or validity check shall end within ≤ 0.2 s.
requirements.baseline_impl: Not met: `commIssue` is SOFT_DISABLE (`selfdrive/selfdrived/events.py:853-856`), soft disable keeps actuating 3 s (`selfdrive/selfdrived/state.py:7-8`); alive allows 10 periods (`cereal/messaging/__init__.py:265`) (GAP-16). FM-03 in WP-C-07 (assurance/02-concept/WP-C-07-sotif-functional-modifications.md)

requirements.text: `controlsd` shall check the age of `modelV2`, `longitudinalPlan` and `carState` before use (≤ 2 nominal periods) and shall set `latActive`/`longActive` false and raise an event when an input is stale.
requirements.baseline_impl: Partly met: `latActive` / `longActive` are false while an input is stale (`selfdrive/controls/lib/input_freshness.py`), but after 10 nominal periods, not 2, to avoid nuisance disengagements from model frame drops until logs show the jitter; the event is `selfdrived`'s `commIssue` from the same 10-period check (GAP-16 narrowed; impact record OI-1)

requirements.text: No diagnostic (`commIssue`, posenet, locationd, `modeldLagging`) shall be masked while the item is engaged, and the driving model shall not be switched while engaged. In the reference configuration the external big model (E-06) shall be absent and not loadable.
requirements.baseline_impl: Not met: masking during big-model load + 5 s (`selfdrive/selfdrived/selfdrived.py:382-384, 403, 457`); hot switch `selfdrive/modeld/modeld.py:411-419` (GAP-17). AIR-25, AIR-30 (WP-C-11 (assurance/02-concept/WP-C-11-ai-system-definition-and-safety-requirements.md))

requirements.text: Non-finite actuator commands shall be treated as a fault with immediate disable, not replaced silently.
requirements.baseline_impl: Not met: replaced by 0 and logged (`selfdrive/controls/controlsd.py:140-147`) (GAP-19)

requirements.text: The SoC controller shall command with margin below every envelope limit: steering torque ≤ 90 % of τ_max(v), acceleration within [a_min + 0.2, a_max − 0.2] m/s² (proposed), lateral acceleration ≤ 3.0 m/s², lateral jerk ≤ 5 m/s³.
requirements.baseline_impl: Partial: 3.0 m/s² and 5 m/s³ (`selfdrive/controls/lib/drive_helpers.py:9-14`); torque and accel limits equal to the envelope (`values.py:20, 39-47`)

requirements.text: On every fault-induced transition to L2/L3 (FSC §12) the SoC shall give a visual and acoustic take-over request within ≤ 1 s of detection, with text that names the actual fault class.
requirements.baseline_impl: Partial: alerts exist (`selfdrive/selfdrived/events.py:224-234`); `canError` shows "Unknown Vehicle Variant" (`events.py:928-936`) (GAP-19); timing not verified

requirements.text: The SoC shall warn the driver when the EPS reports LKA unavailable or faulted (complements TSR-110).
requirements.baseline_impl: Implemented: `steerFaultTemporary/Permanent` → events with 1.5 s hysteresis (`selfdrive/car/car_events.py`, onboard review)

requirements.text: Driver monitoring shall escalate warnings for an inattentive driver with the timing set in WP-C-08 §5 (baseline vision 5/8/13 s, wheel-touch 5/15/25 s).
requirements.baseline_impl: Implemented: `selfdrive/monitoring/policy.py:31-36`

requirements.text: The DM chain shall mark its output invalid when the cabin image or model output is missing or not credible, and an invalid DM output for > 2 s while engaged shall escalate to a take-over request.
requirements.baseline_impl: Not met: `driverStateV2` always `valid=True` at source (`selfdrive/modeld/dmonitoringmodeld.py:99`) (GAP-21). AIR-15, AIR-27

requirements.baseline_impl: Not met: `selfdrive/monitoring/dmonitoringd.py:26-38` (GAP-20)

requirements.text: If the driver does not respond to the highest DM warning, the SoC shall decelerate, disengage and lock out re-engagement for 1/5/15/30 min.
requirements.baseline_impl: Implemented: `selfdrive/monitoring/policy.py:39-44`; `selfdrive/controls/controlsd.py:203-204`

requirements.text: The wheel-touch fallback shall reset awareness only on a deliberate driver input above a defined threshold, not on any steering or gas input.
requirements.baseline_impl: Not met: any steer/gas input resets (`selfdrive/monitoring/policy.py:334-335`) (GAP-21)

requirements.text: Debug, joystick and maneuver modes, and the `lateralManeuverPlan` path to the actuator, shall be absent from reference-configuration builds.

requirements.baseline_impl: Not met: 1 s (`selfdrive/pandad/pandad.cc:78-79`)

requirements.text: The SoC shall immediately disable on any panda fault flag, heartbeat-lost flag, rising `safetyTxBlocked` count while engaged, or SPI error burst reported in `pandaStates`.
requirements.baseline_impl: Partly met: heartbeat lost, LionDriver TX-rate revocation and a rising `safetyTxBlocked` while engaged disable at once (`pandaHeartbeatLost`, `pandaTxRateExceeded`, `pandaTxBlocked`; `selfdrive/selfdrived/supervision.py`), as do `relayMalfunction` and `safetyRxChecksInvalid`. Other fault flags and SPI error bursts: no reaction yet (impact record OI-2)

requirements.text: Driving-model outputs shall be checked for non-finite values, range plausibility and age before use, per AIR-16, AIR-17 and AIR-25 of WP-C-11 (assurance/02-concept/WP-C-11-ai-system-definition-and-safety-requirements.md).
requirements.baseline_impl: Partial: non-finite check on the big model only (onboard review, `selfdrive/modeld/modeld.py:210-211`) (GAP-22)

requirements.text: Excessive-actuation detection (longitudinal outside 2× ACCEL_MIN/MAX, lateral > 2× ISO lateral acceleration for > 0.25 s) shall be kept and shall latch until cleared offroad.
requirements.baseline_impl: Implemented: `selfdrive/selfdrived/helpers.py:12, 30, 41`; latch `selfdrive/selfdrived/selfdrived.py:305-310`

requirements.text: A PCM-reported ACC fault shall cause immediate disable with a take-over request.
requirements.baseline_impl: Implemented: `accFaulted` IMMEDIATE_DISABLE (`selfdrive/selfdrived/events.py:908`)

requirements.text: `pandad` shall compare the panda-reported safety model, safety parameter and alternative experience with the release-record values and shall prevent engagement and raise an alert on mismatch (refines CSR-016 of WP-S-07 (assurance/03-system/WP-S-07-cybersecurity-requirements-architecture.md)).
requirements.baseline_impl: Not implemented: `pandad` sets the values from `CarParams` and does not compare them with a reference (`selfdrive/pandad/panda_safety.cc:56-69`)

requirements.text: The item shall not request the TOYOTA safety mode or allow engagement unless the ECU firmware versions read at start-up (EPS, engine, ABS, radar, camera) match the release record of the reference configuration; an unverified or mismatching firmware set shall keep the safety MCU in NOOUTPUT and inform the driver. The envelope cannot read ECU firmware itself, so the refusal rests on the SoC query plus the mode lock of TSR-512.
requirements.baseline_impl: Not implemented: fingerprinting accepts a fuzzy match and can be forced or skipped by environment (`opendbc_repo/opendbc/car/car_helpers.py:86-87, 144, 164`); no comparison with a release record (WP-A-03 ECU-FW row; TSR-803 is the procedural counterpart)

requirements.text: While engaged, `selfdrived` shall raise an immediate disable with a take-over request when any panda in a car safety mode reports `controlsAllowed` false, after at most 2 consecutive mismatched samples to absorb transport skew between the CAN and `pandaStates` sockets, and in any case within ≤ 0.5 s of the first mismatched sample.
requirements.baseline_impl: Implemented, not verified on the vehicle: `controlsMismatch` after 2 consecutive mismatched `pandaStates` samples and at most 0.5 s after the first mismatched frame (`selfdrive/selfdrived/supervision.py`, unit tests). 2026-10-14: samples in the first 0.3 s after engaging are not counted, because the panda grants authority only on the heartbeat (TSR-301); the 0.5 s bound from the first mismatched frame is unchanged

requirements.text: While the item can engage, the SoC shall supervise the liveness of the HMI path (UI render loop and sound output stream, each with a heartbeat) and treat a missing heartbeat for > 1 s as a fault: immediate disable, with the take-over request carried by the panda siren (TSR-516) and the cluster cruise state (TSR-309, FSR-05.05).
requirements.baseline_impl: Partial: a crashed `ui`/`soundd` raises `processNotRunning` (`selfdrive/selfdrived/selfdrived.py:351-357`); a hung render loop or stalled audio stream is not detected

requirements.text: Alert sound output shall not be muted or set below a defined audible minimum while the item can engage; if the minimum cannot be guaranteed, engagement shall be prevented with a no-entry alert.
requirements.baseline_impl: Not assessed at the baseline (WP-C-08 MC-12)

requirements.text: The SoC shall command deceleration that is not caused by traffic (driver-monitoring no-response, fault-induced force deceleration) only after a visual and acoustic alert announcing it has been given, and shall ramp the request within the envelope bounds a_min (TSR-202) and j_down (TSR-205).
requirements.baseline_impl: Partial: DM escalation alerts precede the no-response deceleration (`selfdrive/monitoring/policy.py`); soft-disable force deceleration is announced at its start (`selfdrive/controls/lib/longitudinal_planner.py:84-85`); jerk not bounded (GAP-04)

requirements.text: Forward collision warnings shall be raised only from fresh and valid inputs (`modelV2` and `longitudinalPlan` within 2 nominal periods, validity flags set), and the false-FCW rate per driving hour in the ODD shall meet a target set in WP-V-02 (assurance/06-validation/WP-V-02-sotif-vv-strategy.md).
requirements.asil: A (open: WP-C-04 OI-9; allocated to the QM SoC)
requirements.baseline_impl: Partial: model FCW from `hardBrakePredicted` and planner FCW (`selfdrive/selfdrived/selfdrived.py:440-445`); no explicit freshness gate on FCW inputs; no false-rate target

requirements.text: While engaged, the SoC shall detect that the envelope does not actuate from evidence other than the envelope's own status report: (a) `pandaStates` older than 2 nominal periods (0.2 s) is treated as a controls mismatch (TSR-621); (b) with lateral control active, the EPS-applied torque (STEER_TORQUE_EPS in `0x260`) not following a commanded torque above a threshold for longer than t_blk; (c) with longitudinal control active, the measured acceleration not following the requested acceleration beyond a tolerance for longer than t_blk. Each leads to immediate disable with a take-over request. Threshold, tolerance and t_blk (≤ 0.5 s) shall be set from fork-owned drive logs so that no false detection occurs in the reference log set.
requirements.baseline_impl: Not implemented. (a): `pandaStates` alive limit is 1 s (WP-S-03 §9). The vehicle-side signals come through the panda RX stream, which is separate from the health report but not independent of the MCU (WP-A-03 (assurance/08-analyses/WP-A-03-dependent-failure-analysis.md) DFI-24)

requirements.text: The alert sound path (`soundd`) shall run with a real-time scheduling priority not lower than that of `ui`, or a worst-case load test (maximum logging, encoding and upload) shall show that alert sound output starts within the TSR-606 budget.
requirements.baseline_impl: Not met: `soundd` sets no real-time priority (`openpilot/selfdrive/ui/soundd.py`); `ui` runs at `Priority.CTRL_HIGH` (`openpilot/selfdrive/ui/ui.py:19`). WP-A-02 (assurance/08-analyses/WP-A-02-coexistence-freedom-from-interference.md) FFI-CM-17

requirements.text: The harness orientation (normal, flipped, not connected) shall be detected before the relay is driven, and CAN routing and relay/ignition pin assignment shall follow it; loss or change of orientation while the relay is driven shall lead to SS-S.

requirements.text: With the relay de-energised, the harness shall connect the forward camera to the vehicle CAN without any active component in the path.

requirements.text: Harness connectors shall be keyed and latched so that partial insertion is detected (not-connected status) or cannot occur.
requirements.baseline_impl: Unknown. HWSR-703

requirements.text: The envelope shall forward every camera-side frame to the car side unchanged, except STEERING_LKA `0x2E4`, STEERING_LTA `0x191`, LKAS_HUD `0x412` and (openpilot longitudinal) ACC_CONTROL `0x343`, and shall forward every car-side frame to the camera side.
requirements.baseline_impl: Implemented: `safety.h:254-290`; `modes/toyota.h:6-36` (static blocking of `check_relay` messages); forwarding before RX validation `drivers/fdcan.h:199-221` (GAP-11)

requirements.text: In the reference configuration the envelope shall not accept from the SoC any frame on the car-side bus that the stock PCS function uses or that only a DSU would send: PRE_COLLISION `0x283`, PRE_COLLISION_2 `0x344`, PCS_HUD `0x411`, and the DSU messages `0x2E6`, `0x2E7`, `0x33E`, `0x365`, `0x366`, `0x4CB` and the bus-1 DSU set; if any is kept for a documented reason, its content shall be restricted to the inactive value.
requirements.baseline_impl: **Met in the reference build** (opendbc `5b5a4ba`): `0x344`, the DSU bus-0 messages and the DSU bus-1 set removed from the Toyota TX whitelist; `0x283` passes with zero payload only (`modes/toyota.h`). `0x411` PCS_HUD refused in the reference build (`LIONDRIVER_REFERENCE`, decision D-1); other builds keep it for radar-ACC alpha longitudinal (IA TX whitelist (assurance/07-supporting/impact/change-2026-10-12-opendbc-toyota-tx-whitelist.md))

requirements.text: On SS-S, any MCU fault, MCU reset, loss of device power or harness supply, the relay shall return to the stock camera-to-vehicle connection.
requirements.baseline_impl: Partial: SILENT/NOOUTPUT release the relay (`main.c:44-54`); power-loss behaviour unverified (AOU-13). **Not met for an MCU hang:** without IWDG the relay stays intercepting and forwarding stops, cutting the PCS path (GAP-43; closed by TSR-501 + TSR-502 + TSR-506 readback). HWSR-502, 502a, 506

requirements.text: Forwarded camera-side frames shall be delivered to the car side without loss and with a latency ≤ 1 ms (TBD from the PCS timing analysis) under worst-case bus and SPI load; forwarding queue overflow shall be detected and reported.

requirements.text: Installation shall be done by a trained installer, and the installation record (R-DEV…R-USR) shall be complete and second-person checked before the first engagement and retained per WP-P-04.
requirements.baseline_impl: Implemented by: WP-O-01 §5; WP-M-04. Status: Template pending (WP-O-01 OI-3)

requirements.text: Before every drive the driver shall perform the pre-drive checks and shall not engage if a check fails (vehicle warning lamps, VSC on, clean camera area, device seated, DM camera unobstructed, no offroad alert, driver fit).
requirements.baseline_impl: Implemented by: OPS-01…OPS-07; WP-O-03 §5. Status: Defined. WP-O-02 OI-2: consider system-side DTC checks

requirements.text: Each driver shall receive the user information and safety warnings before first use and acknowledge them; in the development phase only approved safety drivers shall operate the item.
requirements.baseline_impl: Implemented by: WP-O-03 Part A/B; INS-30. Status: Defined

requirements.text: Field monitoring shall collect and analyse drive logs and driver reports of every installed item, including every disengagement caused by a safety mechanism (`controlsMismatch`, `relayMalfunction`, RX invalid, heartbeat lost, `safetyTxBlocked` > 0), and feed problem resolution and the safety case.
requirements.baseline_impl: Implemented by: OPS-11, OPS-12; WP-O-04; WP-P-03. Status: WP-O-04 pending

requirements.text: Vehicle service actions that can invalidate an AoU or the calibration (alignment/steering/suspension, EPS or ECM/ABS replacement or reflash, windscreen, camera or radar work, tyre size, brake repair, collision repair, battery disconnection, scan-tool sessions, aftermarket accessories) shall trigger the re-verification defined for that action before the item is engaged again.
requirements.baseline_impl: Implemented by: SVC-01…SVC-11. Status: Defined; Toyota service information pending (WP-O-02 OI-6)

requirements.text: The reference-configuration check (INS-21…INS-23), PCS-preservation check (INS-27) and harness inspection shall be repeated at least every 6 months and after any service trigger; harness and camera windows inspected monthly.
requirements.parent_text: SG-07; AOU-09; latent faults of TSR-506
requirements.baseline_impl: Implemented by: PM-01…PM-04. Status: Defined. The 6-month interval is also the latent-fault interval for relay stuck-intercepting until TSR-506 readback and TSR-515 start-up test exist (GAP-43)

requirements.text: Item faults shall be handled by replacement, not repair: defective devices or harnesses shall be quarantined, reported and returned; after replacement the full provisioning and configuration steps shall be repeated.
requirements.baseline_impl: Implemented by: ITS-01…ITS-05. Status: Defined

requirements.text: Only released baselines shall be installed by update; until signed updates exist, automatic updates shall be disabled and updates installed manually, followed by INS-15…INS-23; model-weight changes require SOTIF re-evaluation; envelope changes require the envelope verification evidence; parameters shall be re-checked after each update; a withdrawn release shall be replaced or the item put in dashcam mode.
requirements.baseline_impl: Implemented by: UPD-01…UPD-08; WP-O-05. Status: Defined

requirements.text: On removal of the item the stock camera connection shall be restored and stock TSS functions (LTA/LDA, DRCC, PCS) and the absence of DTCs verified; logs needed for field monitoring retrieved; device data, credentials and identity keys wiped or the device kept under LionDriver control with its history recorded.
requirements.baseline_impl: Implemented by: DEC-01…DEC-11. Status: Defined; key-wipe tool pending (WP-O-02 OI-5)

requirements.text: At end of support of a release, every user shall be informed with the date after which the release must not be engaged.
requirements.baseline_impl: Implemented by: WP-O-02 §7.3; WP-O-05. Status: Defined
